# Buyer Agent Services in Gastonia, NC Find the home, then the right terms.

Ally and her team represent buyers across Gaston County, York County and the Charlotte area. You get local knowledge, a builder’s eye on every showing, and a negotiator focused on your interests.

Talk With a Buyer’s Agent

The short answer

A buyer’s agent represents you, not the seller, when you buy a home. In Gastonia and the rest of Gaston County, Ally Bohanan helps buyers set a budget with a lender, narrow the right towns, judge each house’s condition with a builder’s eye, write and negotiate the offer, and manage due diligence through closing. North Carolina requires a written buyer agency agreement before any offer is made. Ally is licensed in North Carolina and South Carolina.
Updated November 2026

Buyer representation

## What does a buyer’s agent do for you?

A buyer’s agent turns a broad home search into a series of clear decisions. Ally helps you define what you actually need, compares each property on its own facts, prepares offer terms you understand, and keeps every deadline organized after the seller says yes.

- Search strategy built around how you want to live, not just price and bedrooms.
- Showings with honest notes on condition, layout, lot and resale.
- Pricing context from recent nearby sales before you write an offer.
- Negotiation on price, due diligence fee, earnest money, repairs and closing date.
- Coordination with your lender, inspector, insurer and closing attorney.

Good comparison goes beyond photos and asking price. Disclosures, restrictions, recurring costs and access can change from one address to the next. Ally helps you verify them through listing documents, public records and the right professionals.

The difference

## Why does a builder’s eye matter on a showing?

Ally is also the business manager and designer at Bohanan Construction (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/bohanan-construction/>) , which builds custom homes in the area. That background changes what she notices in a house: the roofline and drainage, the age of the mechanical systems, the quality of the windows and trim, and which walls could move in a renovation.

It does not replace a licensed home inspector. It helps you decide which houses deserve an inspection in the first place, and what the inspector should look at most closely. Clients have noticed. Jennifer Grant’s review mentions Ally’s knowledge of renovation and construction as a reason she trusted the advice.

If none of the homes on the market fit, ask whether building makes more sense. Should I Buy or Build? (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/should-i-buy-or-build/>) compares the two paths in a few questions.

The buying process

## How does buying a home in North Carolina work?

Most North Carolina purchases follow the same six steps. The order matters, especially the lender conversation before you fall for a house.

### Talk with a lender

A pre-approval tells you what you can comfortably spend and makes your offer stronger. Ally works with a preferred local lender (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/our-preferred-lender/>) , and you are always free to choose your own. Use the mortgage calculator (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/mortgage-calculator/>) to test rough numbers first.

### Sign a buyer agency agreement

North Carolina requires it in writing before any offer. It sets out Ally’s duties, the length of the agreement and her compensation. You will also review the state’s Working With Real Estate Agents disclosure at your first substantial meeting.

### Narrow the towns, then tour

Start with Find My Carolina Community (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/communities/find-my-fit/>) and the town guides, then tour the homes that fit. Ally sends her current listings (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/featured-listings/>) and new matches as they appear.

### Write the offer

Price is one term among many. Ally helps you set the due diligence fee, earnest money, due diligence period and closing date so the offer is strong without giving away protection you need.

### Use due diligence well

This is your window to inspect, appraise, review insurance, check flood maps, read HOA documents and confirm the survey. You can terminate for any reason during this period, so Ally keeps every task on a calendar.

### Close and get keys

North Carolina closings are usually handled by a closing attorney. Ally stays involved through the final walk-through and the signing, and she is still a call away after you move in.

Due diligence

## What should you check before making an offer?

- County and city limits. Taxes and services change at the line. Gaston County’s rate is 59.9 cents per $100 of assessed value as of July 1, 2026, and each city adds its own. In South Carolina, a primary residence is assessed at 4 percent instead of 6 percent once you apply with the county.
- Flood zone. Homes near the Catawba River, the South Fork and their creeks can sit in mapped flood areas. Look up the address on the NC Flood Risk Information System (<https://fris.nc.gov/fris/>) and get an insurance quote early.
- Well and septic. Common in western Gaston County and outside town limits. Budget for inspections of both.
- HOA and restrictions. Planned communities can limit fences, rentals, boats and exterior changes. Read the documents during due diligence.
- Seller disclosures. North Carolina sellers must give you the Residential Property and Owners’ Association Disclosure Statement. “No representation” is a legal answer, so ask follow-up questions.

Straight answers

## Buyer questions, answered

### Do I need a written agreement to work with a buyer’s agent in North Carolina?

Yes. The North Carolina Real Estate Commission requires a written buyer agency agreement before a buyer’s agent presents any offer for you, written or oral. The agreement spells out the agent’s duties, how long it lasts and how the agent is paid. Ally reviews it with you line by line before you sign.

### Who pays the buyer’s agent?

It depends on what you negotiate. Under NCREC rules, the buyer agency agreement must state the compensation and who pays it. Sometimes a seller offers to cover some or all of it, and sometimes the buyer does. Ask Ally to walk through the options before you sign anything.

### What is a due diligence fee, and is it refundable?

In a North Carolina purchase, the due diligence fee is a negotiated amount paid directly to the seller for the right to inspect and to walk away for any reason during the due diligence period. It is generally not refundable unless the seller breaches the contract, and it is credited to you at closing. Earnest money is separate. It is held in escrow and returned if you terminate within the due diligence period.

### Does Ally help buyers in South Carolina?

Yes. Ally is licensed in both North Carolina and South Carolina. Her Zillow profile shows 14 recorded South Carolina sales as of November 19, 2026, in York County towns such as Clover, Lake Wylie, Rock Hill, York and Fort Mill. Contracts, taxes and closing customs differ across the state line, so she explains each one as it comes up.

### Can I buy a home before I sell mine?

Often, yes, but it depends on your financing. Talk with a lender first about whether you can carry two payments or need your sale to close first. Ally can then plan the timing of both sides and write terms that protect you.

### How long does it take to buy a home in Gastonia?

Searches vary from a few days to many months. Once you are under contract, the timeline is set by the due diligence period and the closing date you and the seller agree on. Debbie Searcy’s review describes finding her home within days and closing within two weeks, which is fast. Most buyers should plan for longer.

# Buy a Luxury Home in Gastonia, NC Luxury, measured in details.

In a luxury purchase, the details decide the value: the craftsmanship, the setting and the privacy. Ally reads all three, and she can tell how a house was built.

Talk With a Buyer’s Agent

The short answer

Buying a luxury home in Gastonia, Belmont or the Charlotte area means judging more than finishes. Ally Bohanan, a Realtor who is also the business manager and designer at Bohanan Construction, evaluates construction quality, setting and privacy, then compares the price with recent sales and with what it would cost to build. As of November 19, 2026, her Zillow profile includes sales up to $4,500,000.
Updated November 2026

Beyond the finishes

## What does Ally look for in a luxury home?

- How it was built. Framing, roofing, windows, waterproofing and mechanical systems matter more than the countertop. Ally knows where builders save money and where they should not.
- The setting. Acreage, water frontage, views and what could be built next door. A quiet lot today can change with one rezoning.
- Privacy. In the showing schedule, in the marketing and in how the home sits on its land.
- Renovation potential. Older and architecturally unique homes can be the best value in the market, if the bones are right. Ally can tell you which walls move and which do not.
- Where the value is. The asking price measured against recent sales and against replacement cost.

The difference

## How is buying a luxury home different?

The buyer pool is smaller and the homes are less alike, so every part of the process needs more care. Fewer comparable sales mean appraisals can come in below contract price, and lenders may treat larger loans differently. Inspections take longer on bigger homes with more systems: pools, generators, docks, wells, outbuildings and smart-home wiring all need a qualified eye.

Some sellers prefer a quiet sale, so not every distinctive home is promoted widely. Ally watches the MLS and stays in touch with other agents. She cannot promise access to unlisted homes, but she can tell you what is likely to come up and when.

The luxury process

## What are the steps to buy a luxury home?

### Define the life, then the house

Setting, commute, schools, privacy and how you entertain. A clear brief keeps the search short.

### Prepare the financing

Larger loans and jumbo programs can have different documentation and reserve requirements. Start the lender conversation early, or line up proof of funds for a cash purchase.

### Tour with a builder’s eye

Ally flags construction quality, maintenance history and renovation potential on each showing, and helps you decide which homes deserve a full inspection.

### Price it against the market and the cost to build

Ally compares recent sales and, where useful, an estimate of what it would cost to build something similar with Bohanan Construction.

### Negotiate and complete due diligence

Specialist inspections, survey, appraisal, insurance and any HOA or lake rules. Ally keeps every deadline in view until closing.

Settings that draw luxury buyers

## Where are luxury homes in this area?

Distinctive homes in this part of the Carolinas tend to cluster around water, historic downtowns and land. Belmont and Mount Holly sit on the Catawba River. Lake Wylie crosses the state line into York County. Gastonia has the York-Chester and Brookwood historic districts, and western Gaston County and Clover offer acreage for custom builds. Charlotte is next door.

## When does building make more sense than buying?

Straight answers

## Luxury buyer questions

### What counts as a luxury home in the Gastonia area?

There is no official price line. In this market, buyers usually mean homes that stand well above the local median for their size, finish and setting: lake or river frontage, acreage, custom construction or a notable historic house. For context, 8 of the 120 sales on Ally’s Zillow profile closed at $750,000 or more as of November 19, 2026.

### Why is pricing a luxury home harder?

There are fewer comparable sales, and the features that drive value, such as frontage, acreage and custom work, rarely match from one home to the next. Ally studies the closest sales, adjusts for real differences and, because she works with a builder, can estimate what it would cost to build something similar today.

### Should I buy an existing luxury home or build one?

Buy if a home already matches most of your list and the price makes sense against replacement cost. Build if you need a specific layout, lot or level of finish that the market does not offer. Should I Buy or Build? (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/should-i-buy-or-build/>) and Bohanan Construction (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/bohanan-construction/>) can help you decide.

### Can you help me buy a luxury home before I move here?

Yes. Many of Ally’s clients relocate from out of state. She can preview homes, send honest notes on condition and setting, and help you plan an efficient visit. See the relocation guide (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/relocation/>) .

### Can I buy and sell a luxury home at the same time?

Yes, with careful timing. Ally can represent you on both sides and coordinate the dates so you are not forced into a rushed sale or a bridge you do not need. Talk with your lender early about financing both.

# Moving to the Carolinas, from anywhere.

Many of Ally’s clients arrive from out of state. Before you ever tour a house, she helps you understand the towns on both sides of the state line.

Talk With a Buyer’s Agent

The short answer

Relocating to the Charlotte area usually starts with one question: which side of the state line? Gaston County, North Carolina sits west of Charlotte, and York County, South Carolina sits to the south. Ally Bohanan, licensed in both states and based in Belmont, helps you compare towns, taxes and commutes, plan an efficient visit and buy with a builder’s eye on condition.
Updated November 2026

Your relocation plan

## How do you plan a move to the Charlotte area?

Six steps, in the order that saves the most time and the fewest surprises.

### Start with how you want to live

Use Find My Carolina Community (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/communities/find-my-fit/>) to narrow the towns, then read the guides. The comparisons (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/communities/compare/>) put neighboring towns side by side.

### Understand the state line

Gaston County is in North Carolina. York County, including Lake Wylie, Clover, Fort Mill, York and Rock Hill, is in South Carolina. Ally is licensed in both states. Taxes, schools and closing customs differ, so ask early.

### Get pre-approved before you fly in

Ally works with a preferred local lender (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/our-preferred-lender/>) , and you can choose any lender you like. A pre-approval means your offer can move when the right house appears.

### Plan your visit around a Saturday

Try Plan My Weekend (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/lifestyle/plan-my-weekend/>) to build a day around the towns on your list, and drive your future commute at rush hour.

### Tour with someone who notices

Honest notes and a builder’s eye on condition, especially if you are deciding before you can walk every house yourself.

### Close from wherever you are

North Carolina closings are usually handled by a closing attorney. Ask the closing office early about remote signing options and wiring instructions.

Two states, one metro

## North Carolina or South Carolina: what changes?

- Property taxes. Gaston County charges 59.9 cents per $100 of assessed value as of July 1, 2026, plus a city rate inside town limits. South Carolina taxes an owner-occupied primary residence at a 4 percent assessment ratio instead of 6 percent, once you apply with the county assessor.
- Schools. Gaston County Schools covers the North Carolina side. York County has separate districts for Clover, Fort Mill, York and Rock Hill.
- Contracts and closing. Each state uses its own purchase forms and customs. In North Carolina, buyers pay a negotiated due diligence fee directly to the seller.
- Lake Wylie. The lake crosses the state line, so two homes on the same water can be in different states. The Lake Wylie guide (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/lake-wylie/>) explains how to tell.

Ask a tax adviser how income tax and vehicle taxes would affect your household before you decide.

Buyers who want land look west toward Dallas, Cherryville and Kings Mountain. Ally can explain how each one feels on an ordinary Tuesday.

Common surprises

## What do relocating buyers often miss?

- Commute times at rush hour, especially on the I-85 and I-485 crossings of the Catawba River.
- Flood-zone status near the river and its creeks. Check the NC Flood Risk Information System (<https://fris.nc.gov/fris/>) .
- Well and septic on rural property, and the inspections each one needs.
- HOA rules in planned communities, from fences to boats.
- Whether building would serve them better than buying. See Should I Buy or Build? (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/should-i-buy-or-build/>)

Straight answers

## Relocation questions

### Is Gaston County in North Carolina or South Carolina?

North Carolina. Gaston County sits just west of Charlotte. York County, which includes Lake Wylie, Clover, Fort Mill, York and Rock Hill, is directly south across the South Carolina line. Many people live in one state and work in the other.

### How do property taxes differ between North Carolina and South Carolina here?

In Gaston County, the county rate is 59.9 cents per $100 of assessed value as of July 1, 2026, plus any city rate. South Carolina assesses an owner-occupied primary residence at 4 percent of value instead of 6 percent, but you must apply with the county. State income taxes also differ, so ask a tax adviser how a move would affect you.

### Can I buy a home before I visit in person?

Some buyers do, but Ally recommends at least one visit to the towns on your list. She can preview homes, share honest notes and help you plan a tight trip. The due diligence period lets you inspect thoroughly before you are fully committed.

### How far are these towns from Charlotte Douglas International Airport?

Belmont and Mount Holly sit just across the Catawba River from the airport side of Charlotte, which is one reason frequent travelers look there. Drive times depend on traffic, so test the route at the hours you would actually travel.

### Do schools change at the state line?

Yes. North Carolina towns are served by Gaston County Schools, and York County, South Carolina has several separate districts, including Clover, Fort Mill, York and Rock Hill. Confirm the assignment for the exact address with the district.

Seller preparation guide

## How to prepare your home to sell

Most of what makes a listing succeed happens before it goes live. This is the order Ally recommends. The timeline tool above turns it into a week-by-week plan.

### 1. Start with a pricing conversation, not a number

Ally walks through the home, studies recent nearby sales and current competition, and explains the range she would list in and why. Online estimates can be a starting point, but they cannot see your kitchen, your lot or the street. That is why Ally prices homes in person.

### 2. Gather your documents early

Mortgage payoff, HOA contacts, warranties, permits, surveys and utility averages. Buyers ask for them, and having them ready keeps the contract moving.

### 3. Repair what buyers will notice

Ally’s construction background helps her separate the repairs that pay for themselves from the ones buyers will overlook. A pre-listing inspection can surface surprises while you still have time to choose.

### 4. Declutter, then stage

Pack what you will not need for a few months. Then stage the rooms that matter most: the living room, kitchen and primary bedroom. See home staging (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/home-staging/>) .

Deep clean, open the blinds, turn every light on, clear the counters and move the cars. Photography day sets the first impression for most buyers.

### 6. Plan for showings

Agree on notice times, a pet plan and lockbox access before launch, so the first weekend goes smoothly.

Disclosures

## What paperwork does a North Carolina seller need?

North Carolina puts more paperwork on sellers up front than many people expect. Before a buyer makes an offer, you must hand over two state forms from the North Carolina Real Estate Commission:

- Residential Property and Owners’ Association Disclosure Statement. Questions about the water and sewer or septic system, roof and structure, plumbing, electrical and HVAC, wood-destroying insects, zoning and covenants, environmental issues and any owners’ association. You can answer No Representation, but you must answer every question.
- Mineral and Oil and Gas Rights Mandatory Disclosure Statement. Whether those rights have been severed from the property.

Before Ally can market your home, the firm must have a written listing agreement with you, and she will review NCREC’s Working With Real Estate Agents Disclosure with you at the first substantial conversation. Gather your survey, HOA documents, warranties, permits for past work and recent utility bills at the same time. If the home has a private well or septic system, find the septic permit and any pumping or repair records; Gaston County Environmental Health keeps permit files.

Under contract

## What happens between the offer and the closing?

Most Gaston County sales use the standard North Carolina Offer to Purchase and Contract. The parts sellers negotiate are the price, the due diligence fee and period, the earnest money, the closing date and possession.

- Due diligence period. The buyer inspects, appraises, surveys and finalizes the loan. The buyer can walk away for any reason before it ends; you cannot.
- Repair requests. Usually arrive near the end of due diligence. Ally’s construction background helps here: she can tell you which items are real, what they are likely to cost and whether a credit makes more sense than a repair.
- Appraisal. If the buyer is financing, the lender’s appraiser checks the price. Pricing with the appraisal in mind avoids renegotiation later.
- Closing. In North Carolina a closing attorney handles the closing and records the deed with the Gaston County Register of Deeds.

Costs

## What does it cost to sell?

Ally walks every seller through an estimated net sheet before listing. The categories are the same for most sales:

- Your mortgage payoff and any home equity line.
- North Carolina excise tax on the deed: $1 for each $500 of the sale price (G.S. 105-228.30), paid by the seller to the register of deeds. On a $400,000 sale that is $800.
- Prorated property taxes for the part of the year you owned the home. Gaston County and city rates are published by the county.
- Repairs or credits you agree to after inspections.
- Listing compensation, which NCREC states is negotiable and must be written into the listing agreement.

In South Carolina the deed recording fee is $1.85 for each $500 of value instead of North Carolina’s excise tax. Your closing attorney prepares the final numbers.

Straight answers

## Selling questions

### How long does it take to sell a house in Gastonia?

Plan on two clocks. Preparation usually takes a few weeks to two months, depending on repairs and staging. After you accept an offer, the contract sets the due diligence period and closing date that you and the buyer negotiate, so the calendar from contract to closing is agreed in writing up front. How fast a home goes under contract depends on price, condition and the competition that month, which is why Ally prices in person rather than promising a number of days.

### What do I have to disclose when I sell in North Carolina?

Under N.C.G.S. 47E, owners of most one- to four-unit homes must complete the NCREC Residential Property and Owners’ Association Disclosure Statement and the Mineral and Oil and Gas Rights Mandatory Disclosure Statement, and give them to the buyer no later than the time the buyer makes an offer. You answer each question Yes, No, No Representation or Not Applicable. If the buyer does not get the forms in time, the buyer may be able to cancel within three calendar days. Some transfers, such as never-occupied new construction, are exempt; ask an attorney if you think one applies.

### What does the due diligence fee mean for a seller?

Under the standard North Carolina Offer to Purchase and Contract, the due diligence fee is paid directly to the seller and is usually credited to the buyer at closing. During the due diligence period the buyer can terminate for any reason, while the seller stays bound. If the buyer terminates in time, the buyer gets the earnest money back but not the due diligence fee, unless the seller breached the contract. NCREC notes that neither fee is required by law; both are negotiated.

### What does it cost to sell a house in North Carolina?

Common seller costs are the mortgage payoff, the state excise tax on the deed ($1 for each $500 of the price, paid to the county register of deeds), prorated property taxes, any repairs or credits you agree to, and the compensation set out in your listing agreement. NCREC is clear that agent compensation is negotiable and must be stated in the written listing agreement. Your closing attorney prepares the final settlement statement.

### Is selling in York County, SC different?

Yes, in a few ways. South Carolina sellers use the SC Real Estate Commission’s Residential Property Condition Disclosure Statement, delivered before the contract is signed unless the contract says otherwise. Instead of North Carolina’s excise tax, South Carolina charges a deed recording fee of $1.85 for each $500 of value, generally owed by the seller. Ally is licensed in both states and lists homes in Lake Wylie, Clover, York, Rock Hill and Fort Mill.

### My home was built before 1978. Is there anything extra?

Yes. Federal rules require sellers of most pre-1978 housing to give buyers the EPA pamphlet “Protect Your Family From Lead in Your Home,” disclose any known lead-based paint information and records, and allow the buyer a 10-day period for a lead inspection unless the buyer waives it. Older homes in historic neighborhoods and mill villages around Gastonia, Belmont and Mount Holly often fall into this group, so check the year built early.

### Should I sell first or buy first?

It depends on your equity, your loan options and how much overlap you can carry. Some sellers make the purchase contingent on their sale, some negotiate a later closing or a short rent-back, and some use bridge financing. Ally plans both sides together and brings in a lender (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/our-preferred-lender/>) early so you know which options are real before you list.

Pricing by hand

## What goes into the price of your home?

- The home itself. Condition, updates, layout, square footage, lot and the systems buyers will inspect: roof, HVAC, water heater, windows.
- Recent comparable sales. Closed sales nearby, adjusted for real differences in size, age, finish and setting.
- Your competition. The homes a buyer will tour the same weekend as yours, and how long similar homes are taking to sell.
- The street and the setting. Traffic, views, water, flood zone, HOA, and whether the home is inside city limits.
- Your timing. What preparation could change, and what the calendar means for buyer activity.

Ally’s construction background helps here. She can tell which updates buyers will pay for and which ones they will discount, and what a needed repair is likely to cost.

Automated estimates

## Why not just use an online estimate?

Online estimates are useful for curiosity and useless for a list price. They cannot see that your kitchen was redone last year or that the house next door needs a roof. They often lag in fast-changing neighborhoods and struggle with unusual homes: acreage, lake frontage, custom construction and historic houses.

Pricing too high costs time on the market, and buyers notice. Pricing too low leaves money on the table. A price Ally can explain is one you can defend when an offer or an appraisal comes in.

Straight answers

## Home value questions

### Is a pricing consultation the same as an appraisal?

No. A pricing consultation is Ally’s professional market opinion of where your home should be listed. A formal appraisal is ordered by a lender and completed by a licensed appraiser, usually after you accept an offer. Ally prices with the appraisal in mind, because a contract price the appraisal cannot support can create problems for the buyer’s loan.

### Why do online home value estimates differ so much?

Automated estimates work from public records and recent sales. They cannot see your updates, your layout, the condition of the roof or the street your home sits on, and different websites use different formulas. Ally uses them only as a starting point for questions, never as the price.

### Is my Gaston County tax value my market value?

Not necessarily. Gaston County last reappraised property in 2023 and schedules its next reappraisal for 2027, so assessed values can lag behind the market in either direction. Buyers and appraisers look at recent sales, not the tax card.

### Does a pricing consultation cost anything?

No. There is no charge and no obligation to list with Ally. If you decide to sell, she will explain the listing agreement and her compensation in writing before you sign anything.

### How soon before selling should I ask for a pricing consultation?

Ideally six to eight weeks before you want to list. That leaves time for the repairs, staging and documents the conversation usually turns up. The selling timeline tool (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/sell-your-home-in-gastonia-nc/#timeline>) works backward from your list date.

Listing representation

## What does a listing agent do for you?

- Pricing. An in-person pricing consultation (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/home-value-in-gastonia-nc/>) grounded in recent sales and today’s competition.
- Preparation. A builder’s view of which repairs pay for themselves, plus staging guidance (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/home-staging/>) for the rooms that matter.
- Presentation. Photography and a listing description that tell buyers what the photos cannot.
- Showings. A schedule that fits your life, with feedback after each tour.
- Negotiation. Price is one term. Ally weighs the due diligence fee, earnest money, financing strength, closing date and repair requests.
- Closing. Disclosures, deadlines, appraisal and repair negotiations, coordinated with the buyer’s agent and the closing attorney.

Selling, step by step

## What are the steps to sell a home in North Carolina?

Six stages, from the first walk-through to the closing table.

### Pricing consultation

Ally walks through the home and explains the range she would list in and why.

### Listing agreement and disclosures

You sign a written listing agreement, review the Working With Real Estate Agents disclosure and complete the state’s property and mineral rights disclosure forms.

Repairs, decluttering, staging and a deep clean, in the order the selling timeline (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/sell-your-home-in-gastonia-nc/#timeline>) lays out.

### Launch

Photography, the listing description and the first weekend of showings.

### Review offers

Ally compares every term, not just price, and negotiates on your behalf.

### Due diligence and closing

The buyer inspects and appraises. Ally handles repair requests and keeps every deadline in view until the closing attorney records the deed.

Straight answers

## Seller questions

### Do I need a written listing agreement?

Yes. North Carolina requires a written listing agreement before a broker markets your property. It sets the list price, the length of the agreement, the broker’s duties and the compensation. Ally reviews every term with you before you sign.

### What disclosures does a North Carolina seller have to give?

Most residential sellers must give buyers the Residential Property and Owners’ Association Disclosure Statement and the Mineral and Oil and Gas Rights Mandatory Disclosure Statement, no later than when the buyer makes an offer. Answering “no representation” is allowed, but Ally must still disclose material facts she knows about.

### What closing costs does a seller pay in North Carolina?

Common seller costs include the excise tax on the deed, which is $1 for every $500 of the sale price, plus the mortgage payoff, any agreed repairs or credits, prorated property taxes and the listing compensation in your agreement. Your closing attorney will give you the final figures.

### What is the due diligence fee, and who keeps it?

The buyer pays the due diligence fee directly to you, the seller, for the right to inspect and to terminate for any reason during the due diligence period. If the buyer walks away in that window, you generally keep the fee. If the sale closes, it is credited to the buyer.

### How quickly will my home sell?

That depends on price, condition, location and the season. Amy Gordon’s review describes going under contract in under six days on one home and under ten on another, and Angel Harris describes multiple offers within days. Those are real results, not a promise. Ally will tell you what she sees in your market.

# Home Staging in Gastonia, NC Staged to be remembered.

Staging helps buyers picture themselves in a home, both online and in person. Ally’s team plans the rooms that matter, from a full furniture plan to simple edits of what you already own.

Request a Pricing Consultation

The short answer

Home staging prepares a house so buyers can picture living in it, first in listing photos and then in person. For Gastonia-area sellers, Ally Bohanan and her team plan staging room by room as part of listing preparation: furniture and décor placement, decluttering and depersonalizing, lighting, paint and accessories, and curb appeal. Ally confirms the scope and any cost for your home before work begins.
Updated November 2026

What’s included

## What does home staging include?

- Furniture and décor placement. Arranging rooms for flow, scale and the angles the photographer will use.
- Decluttering and depersonalizing. Clearing surfaces and packing personal items so buyers see the house, not the household.
- Lighting, paint and accessories. Bright bulbs, neutral touch-ups where needed, and a few well-chosen pieces that add warmth.
- Curb appeal. The front door, walkway, beds and porch, because that is the first photo and the first impression.

Ally and her team actively work to get your property show-ready, and her design work at Bohanan Construction (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/bohanan-construction/>) shapes how she thinks about space, light and finishes.

Staging, in order

## How does staging fit into selling your home?

### Walk-through and pricing

Staging starts with the pricing consultation (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/home-value-in-gastonia-nc/>) , where Ally notes what each room needs.

### Repairs first

Fix what an inspector would flag before spending effort on décor.

### Declutter and pack

Pack what you will not need for a few months. It makes the move easier too.

### Stage the rooms that matter

Living room, kitchen, primary bedroom and the entry, then the rest.

### Clean and photograph

A deep clean, every light on, blinds open, counters clear and cars out of the drive.

### Keep it show-ready

A short daily reset list keeps the home ready for showings while you live there.

Priorities

## Which rooms should you stage first?

Put your effort where buyers look longest. The living room sets the tone of the listing. The kitchen gets the most scrutiny. The primary bedroom should feel calm and uncluttered. After those, give every spare room a clear purpose. A room with a treadmill, a desk and a crib reads as storage.

Outside, trim the beds, sweep the walk, and make the front door look cared for. For homes on acreage or water, the view and the approach matter as much as any room.

Two situations

## Staging an occupied home or a vacant one?

Occupied homes are usually staged by editing: fewer pieces, clear counters, open sightlines and personal items packed away. It costs little and works well.

Vacant homes can feel smaller and colder in photos than they are. Furniture in the main rooms helps buyers understand scale. Ally will tell you whether your home needs it and confirm the scope before anything is arranged.

Straight answers

## Staging questions

### Is home staging worth it?

For most homes, some level of staging is. Buyers decide quickly from listing photos whether to tour, and rooms that are clear, bright and arranged for how people live photograph better. The right amount depends on your home, your price and whether you are still living there.

### Can a home be staged while I still live in it?

Yes. Occupied staging usually means editing what you own: removing extra furniture, clearing surfaces, packing personal items and rearranging for flow and light. Ally will give you a room-by-room list you can work through before photography.

### Which rooms matter most?

The living room, kitchen and primary bedroom carry the most weight in photos and showings. The front entry and curb appeal set the first impression. Spare rooms should read clearly as an office, guest room or bedroom.

### What does staging cost?

It depends on the home and the scope, from a consultation and a to-do list to furniture brought in for a vacant home. Ally will confirm the scope and any cost for your home in writing before work begins.

### Should I make repairs or stage first?

Repairs first, then declutter, then stage, then clean and photograph. The selling timeline (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/sell-your-home-in-gastonia-nc/#timeline>) puts those tasks in order for your list date.

What changes at the top

## How is selling a luxury home different?

- Pricing needs more judgment. Fewer comparable sales, and the features that matter most, such as frontage, acreage and custom work, rarely match.
- Presentation carries more weight. Buyers at higher prices compare homes across the region, often online first.
- Privacy matters. Showings by appointment, buyers qualified before they tour, and care with what the photos reveal.
- Appraisals can be harder. A thin set of comparable sales means Ally prepares notes on upgrades and construction for the appraiser.
- Timelines can run longer. The buyer pool is smaller, so pricing and preparation have to be right from the first week.

The luxury plan

## How does Ally market a luxury listing?

### Pricing consultation

A walk-through with notes on construction, finishes and setting, then a price range grounded in sales and replacement cost.

### Design and staging

Ally, who leads design at Bohanan Construction, edits rooms so the architecture leads. See home staging (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/home-staging/>) .

### Editorial photography

Light, angles and details that show craftsmanship, and video where it suits the home.

### A story buyers can trust

The listing explains what was built, upgraded or restored, in plain language a buyer’s inspector would agree with.

### Private, qualified showings

By appointment, with buyers who are pre-approved or have shown proof of funds.

### Negotiation and closing

Every term weighed, and the appraisal and due diligence managed closely.

Straight answers

## Luxury seller questions

### How do you price a luxury home with few comparable sales?

Ally starts with the closest recent sales, adjusts for frontage, acreage, construction quality and finish, and studies the competing homes a buyer at that price is touring. Because she works with a builder, she can also estimate what it would cost to build something similar today, which is often how luxury buyers think.

### Can my listing be kept private?

There are options for limiting exposure, and each one has trade-offs. A quieter launch protects privacy but reaches fewer buyers. Ally will explain what is allowed under MLS and brokerage rules and what fits your situation.

### Should I stage a luxury home?

Usually, yes. Buyers at higher prices expect a home to photograph and show beautifully. Ally’s design background helps her edit rooms so the architecture and finishes lead. See home staging (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/home-staging/>) .

### Do you also represent luxury buyers?

Yes. Ally represents buyers of luxury and custom homes, including clients relocating from out of state. See buying a luxury home (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/buy-a-luxury-home-in-gastonia-nc/>) .

### Can I sell my current home while building a custom home?

Yes. Ally can time the sale around the construction schedule with Bohanan Construction (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/bohanan-construction/>) . Amy Gordon’s review describes exactly that.

Notary, step by step

## How does a notary appointment work?

### Get in touch

Use the form below or call the office. Tell Ally what kind of document it is and how many people are signing.

### Bring ID and the unsigned document

Each signer needs a current government-issued photo ID. Do not sign before the appointment.

### Sign in front of the notary

The notary confirms each signer’s identity, watches the signature and completes the certificate.

### Take it where it needs to go

Your lender, attorney, county office or the person who asked for it.

Know the rules

## What can a North Carolina notary do, and what can’t they do?

Under N.C.G.S. 10B-20, a North Carolina notary performs four kinds of notarial acts: acknowledgments, oaths and affirmations, jurats, and verifications or proofs. Real estate paperwork usually needs an acknowledgment (for deeds and many closing documents) or a jurat (for sworn statements such as affidavits).

The North Carolina Secretary of State lists things a notary is not allowed to do. A notary cannot:

- certify that a copy is a true copy of an original document
- change or fill in the text of your document
- notarize a photograph by itself (an attached affidavit about the photo can be notarized)
- choose the notarial certificate for you, unless the notary is also a licensed NC attorney
- notarize a document without notarial wording, or with blanks in the certificate
- notarize for someone who does not appear in person, or while outside North Carolina

If your document came from another state or has no certificate wording, ask whoever sent it which certificate they need before your appointment.

Consultations

## Who is a consultation for?

Homeowners thinking about selling in a year or two. Buyers who want to understand the market before they talk to a lender. Families sorting out an inherited property. Owners of land wondering whether to sell or build. Investors weighing a rental.

Ally brings two views to the conversation: a Realtor’s read on recent sales and a builder’s read on condition and cost, through her work at Bohanan Construction (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/bohanan-construction/>) . If building is on the table, Should I Buy or Build? (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/should-i-buy-or-build/>) is a good place to start.

Straight answers

## Notary and consultation questions

### What should I bring to a notary appointment?

A current government-issued photo ID for every person signing, and the complete document, unsigned. Every signer needs to be present. If you are unsure whether your document needs a notary, ask whoever requested it.

### How much does a notary charge in North Carolina?

North Carolina law sets maximum fees. For acknowledgments, jurats, verifications and proofs, a notary may charge up to $10 per principal signature, with higher limits for electronic and remote notarizations. Ally will confirm any fee before your appointment.

### Can a notary give legal advice?

No. A notary who is not an attorney cannot give legal advice, explain the legal effect of a document or choose which form you need. For those questions, talk with a North Carolina attorney.

### What is a real estate consultation?

A one-on-one conversation for people who are not ready to buy or sell yet. Ally can help you understand your home’s market position, weigh selling against holding, plan a purchase or think through land and investment questions.

### Can you notarize closing documents for a home sale?

Ally’s notary services cover real estate documents such as contracts, affidavits and closing paperwork. Your closing attorney or lender may have specific signing instructions, so share them when you book.

### How do I check that a notary is commissioned?

The North Carolina Secretary of State has a public notary search (<https://www.sosnc.gov/online_services/Notary_Search/notary_search>) where you can look up any commissioned notary.

Sources checked November 2026: NC Secretary of State: practice tips on notaries and notarial acts (<https://www.sosnc.gov/divisions/general_counsel/practice_tips_2_notary_and_notarial_acts>) · NC G.S. Chapter 10B: notaries (<https://www.sosnc.gov/documents/forms/notary/Notary_Chapter_10B.pdf>) · NC G.S. 10B-31: notary fees (<https://www.ncleg.gov/EnactedLegislation/Statutes/HTML/BySection/Chapter_10B/GS_10B-31.html>) · NC Secretary of State notary search (<https://www.sosnc.gov/online_services/Notary_Search/notary_search>) . Local knowledge

## What should you know about Gastonia?

Gastonia is Gaston County’s largest city and its county seat, just west of Charlotte along I-85. Its textile history still shapes the city: three neighborhoods are National Register historic districts, Loray Mill, Downtown and York-Chester, and York-Chester and Brookwood are also local historic districts, where exterior changes go through design review.

Downtown, the Franklin Urban Sports and Entertainment District, known as FUSE, is anchored by CaroMont Health Park, which opened in 2021 and is home to the Gastonia Ghost Peppers. Beyond the center, Gastonia ranges from mill-village bungalows to newer subdivisions and land at the edges of the city. The Gastonia guide (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/gastonia/>) covers it in depth.

Straight answers

## Questions about choosing a Realtor

### How do I check a Realtor’s license in North Carolina?

Use the license lookup on the NC Real Estate Commission (<https://www.ncrec.gov/>) website. Ally Margaret Bohanan holds North Carolina broker license 315170 and is associated with Northstar Real Estate, LLC, firm license C29596.

### What is the difference between a Realtor and a real estate broker?

In North Carolina, anyone licensed to sell real estate for others is a broker licensed by the Real Estate Commission. Realtor is a trademark for members of the National Association of Realtors, who agree to its code of ethics.

### Do I have to sign an agreement to talk with a Realtor?

No. A first conversation is free. You will review the state’s Working With Real Estate Agents disclosure at the first substantial meeting, and a written agreement is required before a buyer’s agent makes an offer or a listing agent markets your home.

### What should I bring to a first meeting?

Buyers: your timing, financing status, preferred property type, must-haves and deal breakers. Sellers: the address, your ideal timing, known condition concerns and any documents you already have.

Title: Finding Land & Building on Your Lot | Bohanan Construction

Bohanan Construction · Land and lots

# Finding land and building on your lot

Your land shapes your home more than any finish you choose. Here is what to look at, whether you are still searching or already own a lot.

Talk About My Land

The short answer

Before you build, confirm six things about the land: how it is accessed, which utilities reach it, whether the soil supports septic if needed, its slope and drainage, any restrictions and setbacks, and who handles permits. Bohanan Construction reviews these with you, and Ally, a licensed broker, can help you find and evaluate land first.
Updated November 2026

Starting point 01

## I need to find land

A lot that looks like a good buy on paper can need more work than the listing suggests. Because Ally is a licensed real estate broker and also guides design at Bohanan Construction, she can look at a property with both the purchase and the build in mind, and bring questions to Chantzler before you commit.

Start with the place. The community guides (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/communities/>) describe each town, and the town guides for Gastonia (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/gastonia/>) , Belmont (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/belmont/>) , Mount Holly (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/mount-holly/>) and Kings Mountain (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/kings-mountain/>) cover what to check before you buy there. When you find a property, share it and the team will talk through what it would take to build on it.

Not sure you want to build at all? Should I Buy or Build? (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/should-i-buy-or-build/>) compares both paths using your own answers.

Buying with Ally (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/buyer-agent-services-in-gastonia-nc/>)

Starting point 02

## I already own a lot

Your land is the starting point of the design. Where the sun falls, how the lot slopes, where the road and utilities are, and what the restrictions allow all shape where the house sits and how it is laid out.

Bring what you have to the first conversation: the address or parcel number, a survey or plat, any HOA documents, and photos of the site. The team will help confirm the jurisdiction and site considerations for your build.

The Roosevelt, shown here from the air, is one example of a Bohanan build fitted to a wooded homesite. See The Roosevelt project story (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/bohanan-construction/projects/the-roosevelt/>) .

What the team looks at first

## The site evaluation checklist

Six things to understand about any lot before the design is final. This is a general guide, not an evaluation of a particular property.

- 01

### Access and driveway

How the lot meets the road, any shared driveways or easements, and how long the driveway needs to be. On larger parcels the driveway can be one of the first big decisions.

- 02

### Utilities

Whether public water and sewer reach the lot, or whether the home will need a private well and septic system. Power and internet service to the site are worth confirming too.

- 03

### Soil, perc and septic

If the lot needs septic, the soil has to support it. A soil evaluation (often called a perc test) through the county shows where a system can go and can shape where the house sits.

- 04

### Slope, clearing and drainage

Topography, tree clearing and where water runs during a storm all affect the foundation and grading plan. Flood maps belong in this check as well.

- 05

### Restrictions and setbacks

Recorded covenants, HOA or architectural guidelines, minimum home sizes, and setback lines from the survey or plat decide what can be built and where.

- 06

### Jurisdiction and permitting

Whether the property falls under a city or under Gaston County for permitting. Kings Mountain, for example, spans both Gaston and Cleveland counties, so the exact parcel matters.

Acreage and rural homesites

## More land, bigger decisions

Many Bohanan clients build on acreage, from a five-acre homesite to a property of more than thirty acres. Larger land brings bigger decisions about siting, views, the driveway and private utilities, and the team helps you weigh them.
See the projects (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/bohanan-construction/projects/>)

Straight answers

## Land and lot questions

### What should I check before buying land to build on?

Start with access, utilities, soil (if the lot needs septic), slope and drainage, recorded restrictions and setbacks, and which jurisdiction handles permits. Ally can help you look at a property before you make an offer, and Bohanan Construction can talk through what it would mean for a build.

### What is a perc test?

It is the common name for a soil evaluation that shows whether, and where, the ground can support a septic system. If a lot cannot connect to public sewer, the results can decide where the house and the septic field go.

### Can I build on a lot I already own?

Yes. Many Bohanan clients come to the team already owning land, from neighborhood lots to acreage. The first step is a conversation about the property and what it needs.

### Can Ally help me find land?

Yes. Ally Bohanan is a licensed real estate broker with Ally Bohanan Real Estate. She can help you search for and evaluate land, and coordinate with Bohanan Construction so the lot and the home plan fit together. See buying with Ally (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/buyer-agent-services-in-gastonia-nc/>) .

### Does a big lot change the build?

Usually. Larger land brings bigger decisions about siting, views, driveway length, clearing and private utilities. Bohanan has built on acreage, from a five-acre homesite to a property of more than thirty acres.

Bohanan Construction

## About timelines and pricing

Every custom home is different. Design, permitting, site conditions, selections and weather all affect how long a build takes, so the team discusses realistic expectations for your project instead of quoting a one-size-fits-all schedule.

Pricing works the same way. Foundation type, utilities, exterior materials and finish level all influence cost, and proposals explain scope, allowances, assumptions and exclusions so you can compare decisions with confidence. Coffered ceilings, herringbone floors, stained beams and thoughtful trim are planned early, so they are part of the budget rather than an afterthought.

Comparing a build with buying an existing home? Try Should I Buy or Build? (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/should-i-buy-or-build/>)

Straight answers

## Process questions

### How does building a custom home with Bohanan Construction work?

It starts with a conversation about your goals, land, budget and timing. The team then helps you understand your homesite, shape the plan and selections, and prepares a personalized proposal before a construction agreement.

### How are construction estimates developed?

Each estimate is built from your project: the land and site conditions, the plan and its size, and your exterior and interior selections. Proposals explain scope, allowances, assumptions and exclusions.

### How do finish selections affect the budget?

Finishes are one of the biggest variables in a custom home. Cabinetry, countertops, flooring, tile and exterior materials can change the cost of two homes with the same floor plan. Making decisions early helps the proposal stay accurate.

### How does financing work for a new home?

Most clients use construction or construction-to-permanent financing from a lender. Bohanan Construction is not a lender, but the team can talk you through the process. Ally’s preferred lender (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/our-preferred-lender/>) is a good place to start.

### How long will my build take?

Every custom home is different. Design, permitting, site conditions, selections and weather all affect timing, so the team discusses realistic expectations for your specific project.

# The Roosevelt

A standalone garage-and-living build: an efficiency apartment on one side and a large garage on the other.

Start a Home Like This

The short answer

The Roosevelt is a standalone garage-and-living build by Bohanan Construction in Gaston County, NC. It pairs about 600 square feet of living space, with a full kitchen, a bathroom and a flex space, with a garage of about 900 square feet.
Updated November 2026

The story

## About The Roosevelt

Bohanan Construction introduced The Roosevelt in early 2026 as a standalone build that can serve as a primary home, an addition to an existing homesite, or a getaway on recreational property.

The team describes the vision as dark, moody and masculine. The living side holds about 600 square feet with a full kitchen, a bathroom and a flex space, next to a garage of about 900 square feet with generous ceiling height, built for vehicles, storage and shop work.

Ally and Chantzler shared the build on Instagram as it went up, from the open garage and shop shelving through the finished exterior lit at dusk.

## Who a build like The Roosevelt suits

Bohanan Construction describes The Roosevelt as a build that can be a primary home, an addition to an existing homesite, or a getaway on recreational property. The layout suits a guest suite, a multigenerational arrangement or a hobby space, with the living side and the garage side under one roof.

The build was shared on Instagram as it went up: the introduction in March 2026, the vision in May, an almost-finished update in September and a completion update in November. The photographs on this page come from those posts.

If you are thinking about a second building on land you already own, ask the planning office for your town or for Gaston County what is allowed on your lot before you design it, including any rules for a separate living space. The team can help you bring the right questions to that conversation.

The custom home process

## From consultation to move-in
The full process (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/bohanan-construction/building-process/>)

### Dream and discover

An unhurried first conversation with Chantzler and Ally about who the home is for, what matters most, and your timing. You also get an honest look at budget ranges and next steps.

### Land and location

Whether you own land, are under contract or are still looking, the team helps you understand what a homesite needs before the design is final: access, slope, clearing, drainage, utilities, HOA guidelines, setbacks and permitting.

### Design and selections

Choose a plan to customize or bring your own, then shape the exterior and interior with Ally’s design guidance: exterior materials, roofline, windows and doors, flooring, cabinetry, countertops, tile and lighting.

### Pricing and planning

Your answers become a personalized proposal built from your land, your plan and your selections, with scope, allowances and assumptions spelled out. A construction agreement follows when you are ready.

### Build and welcome home

Permitting and site preparation, regular progress updates, selections installed as planned, and a final walkthrough before move-in. Chantzler oversees construction on site the whole way.

# Where to live in Gaston, York and Charlotte

Eighteen towns on both sides of the state line, written like a travel guide: what each place is like on a Saturday, what to see first and what to check before you buy.

Areas served

## Both sides of the line

The short answer

Gaston County, NC and York County, SC meet at the state line west and south of Charlotte. Ally Bohanan covers both: Gastonia, Belmont, Mount Holly, Kings Mountain, Cherryville, Dallas, Lowell and McAdenville in Gaston County; Lake Wylie, Clover, Fort Mill, York and Rock Hill in York County; and Charlotte, Lincolnton, Concord, Mooresville and Wesley Chapel around the metro. Start with the county, because it sets your tax system and school district, then use the guides below to compare towns. Each one is checked against official town, county and tourism sources.

Straight answers

## Community questions

### What is the difference between Gaston County, NC and York County, SC?

They sit on opposite sides of the state line. Gaston County towns are in North Carolina, west of Charlotte along I-85 and the Catawba River. York County towns are in South Carolina, south of Charlotte around Lake Wylie and the I-77 corridor. The line changes your property tax rules, your school district and which state’s real estate license your agent needs. Ally is licensed in both states. See how to compare towns across the line (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/communities/compare/>) .

### Which towns are on Lake Wylie?

On the South Carolina side, the unincorporated Lake Wylie community in York County is built around the lake, and Tega Cay sits on a peninsula nearby. On the North Carolina side, Belmont reaches the water at South Point, where Duke Energy runs the South Point Access Area. Read the Lake Wylie guide (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/lake-wylie/>) for the difference between lakefront, lake-view and lake-access homes.

### Which school district serves each town?

In Gaston County, every town in our guides is part of one countywide district, Gaston County Schools (<https://www.gaston.k12.nc.us/about-us/list-of-schools>) ; Kings Mountain also reaches into Cleveland County, so confirm which county a Kings Mountain home is in first. York County has four school districts (<https://www.yorkcountysc.gov/939/School-Boards>) : Clover School District (<https://www.clover.k12.sc.us/>) serves Clover and the Lake Wylie area, Fort Mill School District (<https://www.fortmillschools.org/>) serves Fort Mill and Tega Cay, Rock Hill Schools (<https://www.rock-hill.k12.sc.us/>) serves most of Rock Hill, and York School District 1 (<https://www.york.k12.sc.us/our-schools>) serves York and western York County. District lines do not match mailing addresses, so check the exact home on York County’s school locator (<https://experience.arcgis.com/experience/e827d330f20a4508aa6777bf2c0b94e3/page/Find-My-Schools/>) or the Gaston County Schools address search.

### Which towns are closest to Charlotte?

In Gaston County, Belmont and Mount Holly face Charlotte across the Catawba River, and I-85 and US 29/74 carry traffic east from Gastonia, Lowell and McAdenville toward the city. In York County, the Town of Fort Mill places itself about 19 miles south of Charlotte on I-77, and the City of Rock Hill about 20 miles. We do not publish drive times; traffic varies too much. Ally can help you test the drive at the hours you would make it.

### How do property taxes differ between NC and SC?

North Carolina property tax is set and collected by each county; the NC Department of Revenue (<https://www.ncdor.gov/taxes-forms/property-tax/property-tax-rates/county-property-tax-rates-and-reappraisal-schedules>) lists Gaston County at 59.9 cents per $100 of assessed value for 2026–27, with property valued at 100% of its appraised value and reappraised at least every eight years. Towns add their own rate inside town limits. South Carolina assesses a primary residence at 4% of value once the owner applies, and second homes, other residential property and land at 6%, according to the SC Department of Revenue (<https://dor.sc.gov/property/property-tax-exemptions>) ; York County (<https://www.yorkcountysc.gov/789/Tax-Information>) takes the application through its Assessor’s Office. Ask for the combined estimate on any specific address.

Details change, so confirm hours, dates and prices with each source before you go.

# https://allybohananrealestate.com/communities/compare/

Title: Compare Two Communities: Gaston & York County
Summary: Side-by-side comparisons of Belmont and Mount Holly, Gastonia and Kings Mountain, and Fort Mill and Lake Wylie, plus a route to tour both towns in an afternoon.

Compare Two Communities

# Neighbors, side by side

Three comparisons of towns people often weigh against each other. Each one is organized by question, so it reads cleanly on a phone.

See the comparisons Find My Community (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/communities/find-my-fit/>)

The short answer

To choose between Gaston County, NC and York County, SC towns, start with the state line, because it decides your property tax rules and school district. Then pick the corridor you will drive most: I-85, US 29/74 and US 321 in Gaston County, or I-77, SC 160 and SC 49 in York County. Compare towns on that side, and confirm town limits, school assignment and HOA rules for each address.
Updated November 2026

How to compare

## Four checks before you choose

These hold for any pair of towns in our guides, not only the three below.

### Start with the state line

Gaston County towns are in North Carolina; York County towns are in South Carolina. That one line changes how property is taxed. North Carolina counties set their own rates, listed by the NC Department of Revenue (<https://www.ncdor.gov/taxes-forms/property-tax/property-tax-rates/county-property-tax-rates-and-reappraisal-schedules>) ; South Carolina taxes a primary home at 4% of value instead of 6% once the owner applies, per the SC Department of Revenue (<https://dor.sc.gov/property/property-tax-exemptions>) .

### Check the school district by address

Gaston County is one countywide district, Gaston County Schools (<https://www.gaston.k12.nc.us/about-us/list-of-schools>) . York County has four districts (<https://www.yorkcountysc.gov/939/School-Boards>) : York 1, Clover 2, Rock Hill 3 and Fort Mill 4. A mailing address does not settle it, so look the home up on York County’s school locator (<https://experience.arcgis.com/experience/e827d330f20a4508aa6777bf2c0b94e3/page/Find-My-Schools/>) or the Gaston district’s address search.

### Pick your corridor

Think about the road you will drive most. I-85 runs through Kings Mountain, Gastonia, Lowell and McAdenville, US 29/74 also serves McAdenville, and US 321 heads north from Gastonia past Dallas to Lincolnton. In South Carolina, I-77 serves Rock Hill and Fort Mill, SC 160 meets I-77 at Fort Mill, and SC 49 runs from York toward Lake Wylie.

### Confirm town limits and rules

A Fort Mill or Dallas mailing address can sit outside the town limits, and Lake Wylie is unincorporated. Limits change services, town taxes and zoning, and planned communities add HOA covenants. Ask for the parcel record and any covenants before you compare prices.

# https://allybohananrealestate.com/communities/compare/gastonia-vs-kings-mountain/

Title: Gastonia vs. Kings Mountain, NC: Compared Side by Side
Summary: Gastonia and Kings Mountain compared: downtowns, housing patterns, Crowders Mountain and the battlefield parks, with a route to see both in one afternoon.

Compare Two Communities

# Gastonia vs. Kings Mountain

The county seat and its western neighbor along I-85. Gastonia is the bigger city with the larger downtown; Kings Mountain has the ridge, the battlefield and a smaller downtown.

The short answer

The county seat and its western neighbor along I-85. Gastonia is the bigger city with the larger downtown; Kings Mountain has the ridge, the battlefield and a smaller downtown. Both are covered by Ally Bohanan, who is licensed in North Carolina and South Carolina.
Updated November 2026

Question by question

## How they compare

## Housing and lots

### Gastonia

Downtown blocks, mill-village bungalows, established neighborhoods, newer subdivisions and land at the city’s edges.

### Kings Mountain

In-town homes near the historic district and rural property toward the ridge. The city straddles Gaston and Cleveland counties.

## Downtown

### Gastonia

Gaston County’s largest downtown, with 57 Genova Coffee and Lotus Chophouse.

### Kings Mountain

The Joy Theatre and Nutty for Nutcrackers, at 210 S. Piedmont Ave.

## Public outdoor access

### Gastonia

Rankin Lake Park and Martha Rivers Park, with Crowders Mountain State Park just west.

### Kings Mountain

The 4.8-mile Gateway Trail and Kings Mountain State Park across the state line.

## Destinations

### Gastonia

The Schiele Museum of Natural History and its planetarium.

### Kings Mountain

Kings Mountain National Military Park, site of the October 1780 battle.

## First visit

### Gastonia

The Schiele Museum, then downtown for dinner.

# Gastonia, NC Real Estate Gastonia, a field guide to the county seat

Every stop is a few minutes from the last. Start early on event weekends.

Morning

### Downtown on foot

Late morning

### Stowe Park

Afternoon

### The river

Evening

### Daniel Stowe Conservancy

A botanical garden south of downtown on South New Hope Road. In December it lights up for Holidays at the Garden.

## Cherryville’s roads, schools and Saturdays

### Getting around

NC 150, NC 274 and NC 279 all meet in Cherryville, which the city lists among its infrastructure basics. An NCDOT-funded pedestrian plan places the city in the northwest corner of Gaston County and notes that Main Street is an extension of NC 279, the Dallas-Cherryville Highway that runs east toward Dallas. NC 150 is the route north toward Lincolnton.

### Schools and services

Cherryville students attend Gaston County Schools (<https://www.gaston.k12.nc.us/about-us/list-of-schools>) , the same countywide district as Gastonia and Belmont. The district assigns schools by home address and publishes an address search on its school list; families new to the county start with the Student Assignment Office (<https://www.gaston.k12.nc.us/departments/back-to-school-information/how-to-enroll>) .

### Landmarks and weekends

Start downtown at the C. Grier Beam Truck Museum, which tells the story of the local trucking company that grew national. J. Ralph Beam Jr. Heritage Park and the Gazebo Mini-Park host the town’s gatherings, including the holiday tree lighting. On New Year’s, the Cherryville New Year’s Shooters carry on a well-wishing tradition that goes back generations.

Straight answers

## Cherryville questions

### Where is Cherryville?

Cherryville is in the northwest corner of Gaston County, NC, where NC 150, NC 274 and NC 279 meet. NC 279 continues east to Dallas, and NC 150 heads north toward Lincolnton.

### What is the Cherryville New Year’s shooting?

Every New Year’s, the Cherryville New Year’s Shooters carry on a ritual of old-world well-wishing for the year ahead. It is the tradition people most connect with the town.

### Which school district serves Cherryville?

Gaston County Schools. Students are assigned by address, so use the district’s address search (<https://www.gaston.k12.nc.us/about-us/list-of-schools>) for the specific home.

### What should I check on rural Cherryville property?

Outside the city limits, many homes use a private well and septic system. Ask for the permits, the age of the system and any inspection history before you commit, and confirm road access and any easements on acreage.

### What are property taxes like in Cherryville?

Property tax in North Carolina is set and collected locally. The NC Department of Revenue (<https://www.ncdor.gov/taxes-forms/property-tax/property-tax-rates/county-property-tax-rates-and-reappraisal-schedules>) lists Gaston County at 59.9 cents per $100 of assessed value for 2026–27, with the last reappraisal in 2023 and the next scheduled for 2027. Homes inside Cherryville town limits also pay a town rate, so ask for the combined figure on any address you are serious about.

Day to day

## Dallas day to day: roads and the square

### Getting around

The Town of Dallas calls itself the Crossroads of Gaston County, and it sits just north of the I-85 and US 321 interchange. US 321 runs north past Gaston College toward Lincolnton; from I-85, exit 17 is the college’s posted route onto US 321 North. NC 279, the Dallas-Cherryville Highway, heads west to Cherryville, and Gastonia is directly south.

### Schools and services

Dallas is in Gaston County Schools (<https://www.gaston.k12.nc.us/about-us/list-of-schools>) . Assignment follows the home address, so run the exact house through the district’s school search rather than going by the town name. For college classes and workforce training, Gaston College (<https://www.gaston.edu/locations-maps-directions/>) keeps its main campus at 201 Highway US 321 South, inside Dallas.

### Landmarks and weekends

Dallas was named for Vice President George M. Dallas and served as the first county seat. The 1848 courthouse on the square was restored in 2015, and the Gaston County Museum of Art & History fills the 1852 Hoffman Hotel, including what is described as the state’s largest collection of horse-drawn vehicles. The Historic Town Square at 131 N. Gaston St. is where downtown events gather.

Straight answers

## Dallas questions

### Was Dallas the Gaston County seat?

Yes. Dallas was the first county seat, which is why it has a courthouse square. The seat later moved to Gastonia, and the 1848 courthouse in Dallas was restored in 2015.

### Is Gaston College in Dallas?

Yes. Gaston College (<https://www.gaston.edu/locations-maps-directions/>) lists its main campus at 201 Highway US 321 South in Dallas, reached from I-85 at exit 17.

### Is every Dallas address inside the town limits?

No. Some Dallas mailing addresses are in unincorporated Gaston County. Town limits change which services you get and whether a town tax applies, so confirm it on the county’s parcel records before you compare homes.

### Which schools serve Dallas?

Gaston County Schools, assigned by address. Look up the specific home with the district’s school address search (<https://www.gaston.k12.nc.us/about-us/list-of-schools>) .

### What is at the Gaston County Museum of Art & History?

The museum fills the 1852 Hoffman Hotel on the Dallas square. It is known for what is described as the largest collection of horse-drawn vehicles in North Carolina, alongside its art and county history exhibits.

## Lowell between Gastonia and Belmont

### Getting around

Lowell sits on I-85 between Gastonia and Belmont. Go Gaston points visitors to exit 21 or exit 23; at exit 23, Main Street turns right toward Lowell and left toward McAdenville. Lowell-Spencer Mountain Road leads to George Poston Park, and the Lowell Library is at 203 McAdenville Rd.

### Schools and services

Because Lowell, McAdenville and the edges of Gastonia and Belmont sit so close together, attendance lines matter here: check the specific address in the district’s search, and see the enrollment checklist (<https://www.gaston.k12.nc.us/departments/back-to-school-information/how-to-enroll>) for the proof-of-residence documents you will need.

### Landmarks and weekends

First St. hosts events, with Harold Rankin Park and Bob Bolick Park nearby. Woodlawn Mill, built in 1848 on the South Fork, is where the town began.

## McAdenville the other eleven months

### Getting around

I-85 cuts through McAdenville. Go Gaston directs visitors to exit 23: Main Street turns left into McAdenville and right toward Lowell. Drivers also arrive from US 29/74 on the south side. The town covers about 1.5 square miles along the South Fork River, so most daily errands run to Lowell, Belmont or Gastonia.

### Schools and services

McAdenville has no separate school system; children attend Gaston County Schools (<https://www.gaston.k12.nc.us/about-us/list-of-schools>) , assigned by residence. The district’s school list lets you search an address and see the zoned schools before you tour.

### Landmarks and weekends

R.Y. McAden bought the land in 1880 and chartered Springs Shoals Manufacturing in 1881, and the town’s heritage page also tells the story of Edison dynamo No. 31. The Pharr family’s ties to the mill date to 1939. Much of the village is a National Register historic district of about 85 acres, and the town plan describes newer neighborhoods built in a craftsman style. Legacy Park and the greenway along the South Fork are the everyday gathering places.

Straight answers

## McAdenville questions

### What is it like to live in McAdenville during Christmas Town?

The lights run nightly in December, starting with the tree lighting on December 1, and visitors drive and walk through town every evening. Plan errands for daytime and ask neighbors how they handle the traffic, because December evenings are busy.

### Is McAdenville a separate town?

Yes. It is its own incorporated town in Gaston County, about 1.5 square miles on the South Fork River, with its own adopted 2040 town plan.

### Are McAdenville homes historic?

Many are. A National Register historic district covers about 85 acres of the village, and the 2040 town plan describes newer neighborhoods built in a craftsman style.

### Which schools serve McAdenville?

Gaston County Schools, assigned by address. Look up the home with the district’s address search (<https://www.gaston.k12.nc.us/about-us/list-of-schools>) .

### How do you reach McAdenville from I-85?

Take exit 23 and turn left on Main Street. Turning right takes you to Lowell. US 29/74 is the other way in.

Day to day

## Fort Mill on the I-77 corridor

### Getting around

The Town of Fort Mill credits its growth to its routes: Nation Ford Road, the Catawba River, the railroad, US 21 and I-77. Its own profile places the town about 19 miles south of Charlotte on the I-77 corridor. SC 160 meets I-77 at exit 85 near Baxter Village, where SCDOT began rebuilding the interchange in 2024. Downtown and Baxter Village sit on opposite sides of the interstate.

### Schools and services

Fort Mill School District 4 serves the Fort Mill and Tega Cay attendance area and runs three high schools: Fort Mill, Nation Ford and Catawba Ridge. Attendance is set by the home’s address; the district (<https://www.fortmillschools.org/about-us/school-attendance-maps-online-school-locator>) points families to York County’s school locator and confirms assignments at enrollment. A Fort Mill mailing address can still fall in another district, so check the exact parcel.

### Landmarks and weekends

Main Street and the Fort Mill History Museum make an easy start. The Fort Mill Farmers & Artisans Market runs on Saturdays through the warm months, Walter Y. Elisha Park hosts the SC Strawberry Festival and the Christmas Village, and the Anne Springs Close Greenway has more than 40 miles of trails by day pass or membership.
