# Game Day From Gaston County

Four Uptown venues, one college program closer to home, and how to plan a home-game day.

By Ally Bohanan (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/about-ally-bohanan/>)
Reviewed November 19, 2026

Stops

4

Towns

Charlotte

When

Guide · 4 picks, any order

Read

1 min

The short answer

The Panthers and Charlotte FC play at Bank of America Stadium, the Hornets at Spectrum Center and the Charlotte Knights at Truist Field, all in Uptown Charlotte. From Gaston County, most fans drive in on I-85 or Wilkinson Boulevard (US-74). The other option is to park at a LYNX Blue Line park-and-ride and ride the train to Brooklyn Village Station, next to the stadium.
Updated November 19, 2026

One of the quiet advantages of living west of the Catawba is having big-league sports next door. Here is where each team plays and how to plan around a home date.

Sports & Game Day

The stops

Stop 01Charlotte

## Carolina Panthers and Charlotte FC

Both play at Bank of America Stadium in Uptown. Remaining 2026 Panthers home games include November 22 against Baltimore, December 13 against New Orleans, December 20 against Cincinnati and January 3 against Seattle, all at 1 p.m. (Panthers schedule (<https://www.panthers.com/schedule/2026/>) ). Charlotte FC’s 2027 home opener is February 21 at 3 p.m. against CF Montréal (Charlotte FC (<https://www.charlottefootballclub.com/schedule/2027>) ).

Panthers schedule (<https://www.panthers.com/schedule/2026/>)

Stop 02Charlotte

## Charlotte Hornets

Spectrum Center, 333 E. Trade St. Most weeknight home games tip off at 7 p.m. (Hornets schedule (<https://www.cbssports.com/nba/teams/CHA/charlotte-hornets/schedule/>) ).

Stop333 E. Trade St.
Hornets schedule (<https://www.cbssports.com/nba/teams/CHA/charlotte-hornets/schedule/>)

Stop 03Charlotte

## Charlotte Knights

Truist Field, 324 S. Mint St. In the off-season the ballpark becomes Light the Knights (<https://www.milb.com/charlotte-knights/ballpark/christmas>) , running through January 3.

Stop324 S. Mint St.
Light the Knights (<https://www.milb.com/charlotte-knights/ballpark/christmas>)

Stop 04

## Closer to home

Gaston College competes in NJCAA athletics, an easy way to see a game without heading into Uptown.

See every upcoming home date on the Lifestyle calendar (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/lifestyle/events/?cat=sports>) .

Checked against: Carolina Panthers (<https://www.panthers.com/schedule/2026/>) · Charlotte FC (<https://www.charlottefootballclub.com/schedule/2027>) · Charlotte Knights (<https://www.milb.com/charlotte-knights/ballpark/christmas>) . Details change, so confirm hours, dates and prices with each source before you go.

## If you live here

Living west of the Catawba River puts you close to all four Uptown venues without paying Uptown prices for a house. Belmont, Mount Holly and Gastonia all connect to Charlotte by I-85 and US-29/74, and the Gastonia Ghost Peppers play professional baseball in downtown Gastonia. Read the Belmont (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/belmont/>) and Mount Holly (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/mount-holly/>) guides, or the Charlotte guide (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/charlotte/>) if you would rather live in the city. Moving to the area for work? Start with the relocation page (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/relocation/>) .

Straight answers

## Before you go

### Where do I park for a Panthers or Charlotte FC game?

Bank of America Stadium says there are more than 30,000 parking spaces within a 10 to 15 minute walk. It recommends booking ahead through its parking partner, SpotHero, and arriving early (Bank of America Stadium (<https://www.bankofamericastadium.com/stadium/parking.html>) ).

### Can I take the light rail to the stadium?

Yes. Park at any LYNX Blue Line Park & Ride and ride to Brooklyn Village Station, just over a football field from the stadium. A round trip is $4.40 in the CATS-Pass app, with Park & Ride parking included, and security checks tickets (Bank of America Stadium (<https://www.bankofamericastadium.com/stadium/parking.html>) ).

### Is there a bus from Gastonia or Belmont?

CATS Route 85x, the Gastonia Express, runs between Gastonia, a park-and-ride at Abbey Plaza in Belmont, and Uptown Charlotte (City of Belmont (<https://www.cityofbelmont.org/bus/>) ). It is a weekday commuter route (CATS (<https://www.charlottenc.gov/CATS/Ride/Bus/85x>) ), so it does not help with most weekend games.

### How do I drive in from I-85?

From the Gaston County side, the stadium’s directions say to exit I-85 at Billy Graham Parkway, Freedom Drive, the Brookshire Freeway (I-277 East) or I-77 South. From Wilkinson Boulevard (US-74), follow signs for the John Belk Freeway (I-277) (Bank of America Stadium (<https://www.bankofamericastadium.com/stadium/parking.html>) ).

Facts in these answers checked November 19, 2026 against: Bank of America Stadium: traffic and parking (<https://www.bankofamericastadium.com/stadium/parking.html>) · City of Belmont: bus routes (<https://www.cityofbelmont.org/bus/>) · CATS: Route 85x Gastonia Express (<https://www.charlottenc.gov/CATS/Ride/Bus/85x>) . Hours, fees and dates change, so confirm with each source before you go.

Title: Getting on Lake Wylie Without a Lake House
Summary: Public shoreline, a marina and a creek launch on the North Carolina side of the lake.

Lake Life & Outdoors (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/lifestyle/lake-life-and-outdoors/>) Lifestyle (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/lifestyle/>) · Lake Wylie

# Getting on Lake Wylie Without a Lake House

Public shoreline, a marina and a creek launch on the North Carolina side of the lake.

By Ally Bohanan (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/about-ally-bohanan/>)
Reviewed November 19, 2026

Stops

3

Towns

Belmont, Lake Wylie, Mount Holly

When

Guide · 3 picks, any order

Read

1 min

The short answer

On the Gaston County side, there are three easy ways onto Lake Wylie without owning a dock. South Point Access in Belmont has public shoreline for $7 per vehicle. Tailrace Marina in Mount Holly has boating and paddling access, and River Street Park in Mount Holly has a canoe and kayak launch onto Dutchman’s Creek.
Updated November 19, 2026

You do not need a dock to spend a day on Lake Wylie. The lake covers about 13,443 acres with roughly 325 miles of shoreline (SC DNR (<https://dnr.sc.gov/lakes/wylie/description.html>) ), and the Gaston County side has three easy ways in.

Lake Life & Outdoors

The stops

Stop 01Belmont

## South Point Access, Belmont

A sandy stretch of public Lake Wylie shoreline, and the closest thing Gaston County has to a lake beach (Go Gaston (<https://www.gogastonnc.org/belmont>) ).

Go Gaston (<https://www.gogastonnc.org/belmont>)

Stop 02Mount Holly

## Tailrace Marina, Mount Holly

Boating and paddling amenities with access to Lake Wylie (Go Gaston (<https://www.gogastonnc.org/mount-holly>) ).

Go Gaston (<https://www.gogastonnc.org/mount-holly>)

Stop 03Mount Holly

## River Street Park, Mount Holly

A natural canoe and kayak launch onto Dutchman’s Creek, plus walking trails, fishing and a nine-hole disc golf course.

Checked against: SC DNR: Lake Wylie (<https://dnr.sc.gov/lakes/wylie/description.html>) · Go Gaston: Belmont (<https://www.gogastonnc.org/belmont>) · Go Gaston: Mount Holly (<https://www.gogastonnc.org/mount-holly>) . Details change, so confirm hours, dates and prices with each source before you go.

## If you live here

Lakefront, lake-view and lake-access are three different things, and the difference shows up in price, insurance and how often you actually get on the water. The public access points above are what lake life looks like for many people on the Gaston County side. Read the Lake Wylie guide (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/lake-wylie/>) to understand the shore, the community and the state line, and the waterfront buyer tips (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/waterfront-homes-on-lake-wylie-buyer-tips-2026/>) before you tour a home on the water. Ally’s buyer-agent services (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/buyer-agent-services-in-gastonia-nc/>) cover lake homes on both sides of the line.

Lake WylieCommunity guide (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/lake-wylie/>)

BelmontCommunity guide (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/belmont/>)

Mount HollyCommunity guide (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/mount-holly/>)

Straight answers

## Before you go

### What does South Point Access cost, and when is it open?

$7 per vehicle and $20 per bus. It is open 6 a.m. to 9 p.m. from April 1 through October 31, and 6 a.m. to 7 p.m. from November 1 through March 31 (Gaston County (<https://www.gastongov.com/Facilities/Facility/Details/South-Point-Access-51>) ).

### Can I swim at South Point?

Gaston County opens the swim beach from Memorial Day through Labor Day only. Pets are not allowed in the beach area, and dogs elsewhere in the park must be on a leash six feet or shorter (Gaston County (<https://www.gastongov.com/Facilities/Facility/Details/South-Point-Access-51>) ).

### Where do I park at Tailrace Marina?

Tailrace Marina, 1010 Marina Village Drive, Mount Holly, says it has ample parking shared with JR Cash Grill & Bar (Tailrace Marina (<https://www.tailracemarina.com/>) ).

### Is Lake Wylie in North Carolina or South Carolina?

Both. SC DNR describes Lake Wylie as being on the border between the two states, between Rock Hill and Charlotte. About 7,316 of its acres are in South Carolina, and the lake is owned and managed by Duke Energy (SC DNR (<https://dnr.sc.gov/lakes/wylie/description.html>) ).

Facts in these answers checked November 19, 2026 against: Gaston County: South Point Access (<https://www.gastongov.com/Facilities/Facility/Details/South-Point-Access-51>) · Tailrace Marina (<https://www.tailracemarina.com/>) · SC DNR: Lake Wylie (<https://dnr.sc.gov/lakes/wylie/description.html>) . Hours, fees and dates change, so confirm with each source before you go.

# Trails From Crowders Mountain to the Catawba

Seven trail systems within reach of Ally’s office, from a summit climb to a 2,100-acre greenway.

By Ally Bohanan (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/about-ally-bohanan/>)
Reviewed November 19, 2026

Stops

7

Towns

Kings Mountain, Lowell, Mount Holly, Belmont, Fort Mill, Charlotte

When

Guide · 7 picks, any order

Read

1 min

The short answer

For a summit, hike Crowders Mountain State Park or the 4.8-mile Gateway Trail in Kings Mountain. For something paved and easy, walk the RiverHawk Greenway in Mount Holly. For a full day, go to the Anne Springs Close Greenway in Fort Mill or the U.S. National Whitewater Center on the Catawba River.
Updated November 19, 2026

Trail access is one of the first things relocating buyers ask Ally about. These are the systems worth knowing, with the distances their managers publish.

Lake Life & Outdoors

The stops

Stop 01

## Crowders Mountain State Park

The Crowders Mountain Trail runs 2.5 miles one way, and the Backside Trail is a steep half-mile to the top (Go Gaston (<https://www.gogastonnc.org/gastonia>) ).

Go Gaston (<https://www.gogastonnc.org/gastonia>)

Stop 02Kings Mountain

## Gateway Trail, Kings Mountain

A 4.8-mile trail on the Kings Mountain side of the range (Go Gaston (<https://www.gogastonnc.org/kings-mountain>) ).

Go Gaston (<https://www.gogastonnc.org/kings-mountain>)

Stop 03Lowell

## George Poston Park, Lowell

About 12 miles of trails near the South Fork River (Go Gaston (<https://www.gogastonnc.org/lowell>) ).

Go Gaston (<https://www.gogastonnc.org/lowell>)

Stop 04Mount Holly

## RiverHawk Greenway, Mount Holly

A paved, accessible greenway along the Catawba River and part of the Carolina Thread Trail. It starts at Tuckaseegee Park.

Stop 05Belmont

## Rocky Branch Park, Belmont

Belmont’s mountain-bike trails.

Stop 06Fort Mill

## Anne Springs Close Greenway, Fort Mill

2,100 acres with more than 40 miles of trails, at 2573 Lake Haigler Dr. Entry is by day pass or membership (ASC Greenway (<https://www.ascgreenway.org/>) ).

Stop2573 Lake Haigler Dr.
ASC Greenway (<https://www.ascgreenway.org/>)

Stop 07Charlotte

## U.S. National Whitewater Center, Charlotte

More than 1,300 acres and 40–50 miles of trails on the Catawba (Whitewater Center (<https://whitewater.org/maps/>) ).

Whitewater Center (<https://whitewater.org/maps/>)

Checked against: Go Gaston (<https://www.gogastonnc.org/>) · Anne Springs Close Greenway (<https://www.ascgreenway.org/>) · U.S. National Whitewater Center (<https://whitewater.org/maps/>) . Details change, so confirm hours, dates and prices with each source before you go.

## If you live here

Trail access is one of the first things relocating buyers ask Ally about. In this part of the Carolinas, the answer depends on the town. Kings Mountain is closest to the Crowders and Gateway trails. Mount Holly has the RiverHawk Greenway on the Catawba River, Lowell has George Poston Park near the South Fork River, and Fort Mill has the Anne Springs Close Greenway. Read the Kings Mountain (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/kings-mountain/>) , Mount Holly (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/mount-holly/>) , Lowell (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/lowell/>) and Fort Mill (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/fort-mill/>) guides, then see how Ally helps on the relocation page (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/relocation/>) .

Straight answers

## Before you go

### Do I have to pay to use these trails?

Some charge a fee. A non-member day pass at the Anne Springs Close Greenway is $17 for adults and $8 for youth ages 3 to 12. Members and children 2 and under get in free, and only cards are accepted at the welcome stations (ASC Greenway (<https://www.ascgreenway.org/visit/hours-fees/>) ). Check each park’s official page before you go, because fees change.

### Can I bring my dog?

At the Anne Springs Close Greenway, friendly leashed dogs are welcome on the outdoor spaces at no extra cost, but the dog park needs an add-on membership (ASC Greenway (<https://www.ascgreenway.org/visit/hours-fees/>) ). George Poston Park in Lowell (Gaston County (<https://www.gastongov.com/Facilities/Facility/Details/George-Poston-Park-6>) ) and Tuckaseege Park in Mount Holly (City of Mount Holly (<https://www.mtholly.us/departments/parks___recreation/parks_greenways___trails/parks.php>) ) both have dog parks.

### Which trails are paved or accessible?

The RiverHawk Greenway in Mount Holly is paved and accessible, and part of the Carolina Thread Trail. George Poston Park has a lakeside paved ADA walkway (Gaston County (<https://www.gastongov.com/Facilities/Facility/Details/George-Poston-Park-6>) ).

### When do the trails close?

Crowders Mountain gates close at 6 p.m. from November through February and later the rest of the year, and the park is closed on Christmas Day (NC State Parks (<https://www.ncparks.gov/state-parks/crowders-mountain-state-park>) ). The Anne Springs Close Greenway is open from 7 a.m. until sunset and closes on Thanksgiving and Christmas Day (ASC Greenway (<https://www.ascgreenway.org/visit/hours-fees/>) ).

Facts in these answers checked November 19, 2026 against: NC State Parks: Crowders Mountain (<https://www.ncparks.gov/state-parks/crowders-mountain-state-park>) · Anne Springs Close Greenway: hours and fees (<https://www.ascgreenway.org/visit/hours-fees/>) · Gaston County: George Poston Park (<https://www.gastongov.com/Facilities/Facility/Details/George-Poston-Park-6>) · City of Mount Holly: parks (<https://www.mtholly.us/departments/parks___recreation/parks_greenways___trails/parks.php>) . Hours, fees and dates change, so confirm with each source before you go.

Title: Holiday Lights Across Gaston and York
Summary: Christmas Town USA, garden lights, a ballpark glow and ChristmasVille. The annual traditions, with this year’s dates.

Local Events (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/lifestyle/events/>) Lifestyle (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/lifestyle/>) · Gaston & York counties

# Holiday Lights Across Gaston and York

Christmas Town USA, garden lights, a ballpark glow and ChristmasVille. The annual traditions, with this year’s dates.

By Ally Bohanan (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/about-ally-bohanan/>)
Reviewed November 19, 2026

Stops

5

Towns

McAdenville, Belmont, Rock Hill, Charlotte

When

Guide · 5 picks, any order

Read

1 min

The short answer

These are the four big traditions. Christmas Town USA in McAdenville glows nightly from 5:30 to 10 p.m., December 1 through 26. Holidays at the Garden lights Daniel Stowe Conservancy in Belmont on select nights from November 28 to December 30. Light the Knights runs at Truist Field in Charlotte through January 3, and ChristmasVille fills Old Town Rock Hill in early December.
Updated November 19, 2026

December is when this part of the Carolinas shows off. These are the traditions worth planning around, with 2026 dates from each organizer.

Local Events

The stops

Stop 01McAdenville

## Christmas Town USA, McAdenville

The lights run nightly from 5:30 to 10 p.m. through December 26. The tree lighting is December 1, and the Yule Log Parade, a tradition since 1949, is December 10 (Town of McAdenville (<https://townofmcadenville.org/visitors/christmas-town-usa/>) ).

Town of McAdenville (<https://townofmcadenville.org/visitors/christmas-town-usa/>)

Stop 02Belmont

## Holidays at the Garden, Belmont

Daniel Stowe Conservancy lights up on select nights from November 28 to December 30, 5 to 10 p.m. (Daniel Stowe Conservancy (<https://danielstoweconservancy.org/visit/holidays/>) ).

Daniel Stowe Conservancy (<https://danielstoweconservancy.org/visit/holidays/>)

Stop 03Belmont

## Festival of Trees, Belmont

Stowe Park, December 1–31, free (Downtown Belmont (<https://downtownbelmont.org/festival-of-trees/>) ).

Downtown Belmont (<https://downtownbelmont.org/festival-of-trees/>)

Stop 04Rock Hill

## ChristmasVille, Rock Hill

December 3–6 in Old Town, opening at Fountain Park on December 3 at 6 p.m. (ChristmasVille (<https://www.christmasvillerockhill.com/>) ).

ChristmasVille (<https://www.christmasvillerockhill.com/>)

Stop 05Charlotte

## Light the Knights, Charlotte

Truist Field, November 25 through January 3 (Charlotte Knights (<https://www.milb.com/charlotte-knights/ballpark/christmas>) ).

Every parade and tree lighting, with times and venues, is on the events calendar (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/lifestyle/events/>) .

Charlotte Knights (<https://www.milb.com/charlotte-knights/ballpark/christmas>)

Checked against: Town of McAdenville (<https://townofmcadenville.org/visitors/christmas-town-usa/>) · Daniel Stowe Conservancy (<https://danielstoweconservancy.org/visit/holidays/>) · ChristmasVille (<https://www.christmasvillerockhill.com/>) . Details change, so confirm hours, dates and prices with each source before you go.

## If you live here

For families who live nearby, these traditions turn into weeknight plans instead of road trips. McAdenville is between Gastonia and Belmont along I-85, Daniel Stowe Conservancy is just south of downtown Belmont, and ChristmasVille is in Old Town Rock Hill. Read the McAdenville (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/mc-adenville/>) , Belmont (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/belmont/>) and Rock Hill (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/rock-hill/>) guides. Thinking of listing in the new year? The selling page (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/sell-your-home/>) explains how Ally prepares a home for a winter or spring market.

McAdenvilleCommunity guide (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/mc-adenville/>)

BelmontCommunity guide (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/belmont/>)

Rock HillCommunity guide (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/rock-hill/>)

CharlotteCommunity guide (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/charlotte/>)

Straight answers

## Before you go

### How much are Holidays at the Garden tickets?

A date-specific general ticket is $28 for adults and $25 for children 2 to 12. Value Nights, Monday through Thursday, are $24 and $18, and children under 2 are free. An Any Night ticket is $33 and can be rescheduled to any open date. General tickets are non-refundable. Members get 15% off, and parking is free (Daniel Stowe Conservancy (<https://danielstoweconservancy.org/visit/holidays/>) ).

### What time should I arrive at Holidays at the Garden?

Entry starts at 5 p.m., and the last admission is 9 p.m. You can stay at your own pace until 10 p.m. (Daniel Stowe Conservancy (<https://danielstoweconservancy.org/visit/holidays/>) ).

### Can I walk Christmas Town USA, or is it drive-through?

Both. The Town of McAdenville says you can drive through town or park and stroll. The lights shine from 5:30 to 10 p.m. each night, December 1 to 26, 2026 (Town of McAdenville (<https://townofmcadenville.org/visitors/christmas-town-usa/>) ).

### What does a Light the Knights ticket include?

General Admission covers the light show, the holiday scenes and the market. The All Activities Pass adds skating, snow tubing and more, and these passes are limited each night. Tickets are good any time during your date’s hours, with no re-entry (Charlotte Knights (<https://www.milb.com/charlotte-knights/ballpark/christmas>) ).

Facts in these answers checked November 19, 2026 against: Town of McAdenville: Christmas Town USA (<https://townofmcadenville.org/visitors/christmas-town-usa/>) · Daniel Stowe Conservancy: Holidays at the Garden (<https://danielstoweconservancy.org/visit/holidays/>) · Charlotte Knights: Light the Knights (<https://www.milb.com/charlotte-knights/ballpark/christmas>) . Hours, fees and dates change, so confirm with each source before you go.

Food & Drink (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/lifestyle/food-and-drink/>) Lifestyle (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/lifestyle/>) · Gaston & York counties

# Main Street Coffee and Bookshops

Where to sit with a cup and a new book in Mount Holly, Gastonia, Kings Mountain, Clover and York.

By Ally Bohanan (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/about-ally-bohanan/>)
Reviewed November 19, 2026

Stops

5

Towns

Mount Holly, Gastonia, Kings Mountain, Belmont, Clover, York

When

Guide · 5 picks, any order

Read

1 min

The short answer

Mount Holly has the best pairing, with Cleary’s Bookstore and Black Sheep Coffee sharing 104 S. Main St. and Owl Legs Coffee nearby. After that, try Belmont Bookshop, 57 Genova Coffee in Gastonia, The Social House by Royal T in Kings Mountain, Brick & Mortar Coffee in Clover and Books-4-Ewe in York.
Updated November 19, 2026

A good Main Street has a coffee counter and a bookshop within a few doors of each other. These towns have both. Every listing comes from current tourism or town listings; check hours before you go.

Food & Drink

The stops

Stop 01Mount Holly

## Mount Holly

Cleary’s Bookstore, a woman-owned independent shop, shares 104 S. Main St. with Black Sheep Coffee. Owl Legs Coffee at 101 W. Central Ave. is veteran-owned and inspired by Berlin’s coffee culture (Go Gaston (<https://www.gogastonnc.org/mount-holly>) ).

Stop104 S. Main St.
Go Gaston (<https://www.gogastonnc.org/mount-holly>)

Stop 02Gastonia

## Gastonia

57 Genova Coffee, 167 W. Main Ave. (Go Gaston (<https://www.gogastonnc.org/gastonia>) ).

Stop167 W. Main Ave.
Go Gaston (<https://www.gogastonnc.org/gastonia>)

Stop 03Kings Mountain

## Kings Mountain

The Social House by Royal T, 212 S. Railroad Ave. (Go Gaston (<https://www.gogastonnc.org/kings-mountain>) ).

Stop212 S. Railroad Ave.
Go Gaston (<https://www.gogastonnc.org/kings-mountain>)

Stop 04Belmont

## Belmont

Belmont Bookshop hosts story time and book clubs downtown (Go Gaston (<https://www.gogastonnc.org/belmont>) ).

Go Gaston (<https://www.gogastonnc.org/belmont>)

Stop 05Clover

## Clover and York

Brick & Mortar Coffee in Clover, and Books-4-Ewe on Congress Street in York (Visit York County (<https://www.visityorkcounty.com/>) ).

Visit York County (<https://www.visityorkcounty.com/>)

Checked against: Go Gaston (<https://www.gogastonnc.org/>) · Visit York County (<https://www.visityorkcounty.com/>) . Details change, so confirm hours, dates and prices with each source before you go.

## If you live here

A walkable Main Street with a coffee counter is one of the most common wishes Ally hears from buyers. It can also shape what you pay and how a home resells. Read how walkability affects home values (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/how-walkability-impacts-home-values-in-gastonia-nc/>) , then the Mount Holly (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/mount-holly/>) , Clover (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/clover/>) and York (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/york/>) guides. CloverCommunity guide (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/clover/>)

YorkCommunity guide (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/york/>)

GastoniaCommunity guide (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/gastonia/>)

Straight answers

## Before you go

### When is Cleary’s Bookstore open?

Tuesday to Thursday 9 a.m. to 7 p.m., Friday and Saturday 8 a.m. to 6 p.m., and Sunday 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. It is closed on Mondays. Book clubs meet Thursday evenings from 7 to 9 p.m. (Cleary’s Bookstore (<https://www.clearysbookstore.com/>) ).

### When is Brick & Mortar Coffee in Clover open?

Monday to Friday 6:30 a.m. to 8 p.m., Saturday 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. and Sunday 8 a.m. to 2 p.m., at 109 N. Main St. Holiday hours are shorter, and it closes on Christmas Day (Brick & Mortar Coffee (<https://www.brickandmortarcoffeesc.com/our-location>) ).

### Which of these towns are in South Carolina?

Clover and York are in York County, South Carolina. Mount Holly, Belmont, Gastonia and Kings Mountain are in Gaston County, North Carolina. Clover is a short drive from Kings Mountain and Gastonia across the state line, so you can easily visit both in one Saturday.

### Are these shops independent?

Go Gaston describes Cleary’s as a woman-owned independent bookstore and Owl Legs Coffee as veteran-owned (Go Gaston (<https://www.gogastonnc.org/mount-holly>) ). Books-4-Ewe is an independent bookstore on Congress Street in York.

Facts in these answers checked November 19, 2026 against: Cleary’s Bookstore (<https://www.clearysbookstore.com/>) · Brick & Mortar Coffee (<https://www.brickandmortarcoffeesc.com/our-location>) . Hours, fees and dates change, so confirm with each source before you go.

# https://allybohananrealestate.com/lifestyle/a-day-in-york-county-history/

Nearly 200 registered sites in York, an 800-acre living-history farm and Rock Hill’s Mural Mile.

The short answer

Start at Historic Brattonsville, an 800-acre living-history site near McConnells that is open Tuesday to Saturday. Then walk Congress Street in York, and finish in Old Town Rock Hill with the Mural Mile and Glencairn Garden, which is free and open daily from dawn to dusk.
Updated November 19, 2026

York County, South Carolina, keeps its history close to the surface. This day moves from a living-history farm to a historic downtown, and ends with murals in Old Town Rock Hill.

## If you live here

York, Rock Hill and Fort Mill sit on the South Carolina side of the Charlotte region, and each has a different pace. York is a small historic county seat, Rock Hill is a college city with an active Old Town, and Fort Mill is close to the state line. Read the Rock Hill neighborhood guide for relocating buyers (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/rock-hill-sc-neighborhood-guide-relocating-buyers/>) , then see how Ally helps with a move across the state line on the relocation page (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/relocation/>) .

Straight answers

## Before you go

### What does Historic Brattonsville cost, and when is it open?

Admission is $12 for adults 18 to 59, $10 for seniors 60 and up and $8 for youth 4 to 17. Members and children 3 and younger get in free. Hours are Tuesday to Saturday 10 a.m. to 5 p.m. and Sunday 1 to 5 p.m. for self-guided tours, and it is closed on Mondays. Online ticket sales end at 3 p.m. and walk-up sales at 4 p.m. (Culture & Heritage Museums (<https://chmuseums.org/plan-your-visit-hb/>) ).

### Can I bring my dog to Brattonsville?

No. Pets are not permitted, but service animals are always welcome (Culture & Heritage Museums (<https://chmuseums.org/plan-your-visit-hb/>) ).

### Does Glencairn Garden charge admission?

No. The City of Rock Hill lists no admission fee, and the garden at 725 Crest Street is open daily from dawn to dusk. Group tours can be arranged through the York County Master Gardeners (City of Rock Hill (<https://www.cityofrockhill.com/Home/Components/FacilityDirectory/FacilityDirectory/86/151>) ).

### Where are the Mural Mile murals?

They are spread across Old Town Rock Hill. Locations include 121, 157 and 212 East Main Street, the York County Library at 153 East White Street, and 130 West White Street (Visit Rock Hill (<https://www.visitrockhillsc.com/mural-mile/>) ).

Facts in these answers checked November 19, 2026 against: Historic Brattonsville: plan your visit (<https://chmuseums.org/plan-your-visit-hb/>) · City of Rock Hill: Glencairn Garden (<https://www.cityofrockhill.com/Home/Components/FacilityDirectory/FacilityDirectory/86/151>) · Visit Rock Hill: Mural Mile (<https://www.visitrockhillsc.com/mural-mile/>) . Hours, fees and dates change, so confirm with each source before you go.

### How often is the Journal updated?

New articles are added regularly and older ones are reviewed and revised. Every article shows its published date, plus an “Updated” date when it has been revised, and the newest articles are always at the top of this page. There are 193 articles today.

### Are the market articles based on local sales data?

Not on their own. Market articles explain trends in plain language and link the public sources they cite, such as the U.S. Census Bureau or Freddie Mac’s weekly mortgage rate survey. They are not MLS statistics. The Journal · Selling59 articles

# Selling a Home in Gaston County

Pricing, preparation, staging, offers and closing for sellers.

About this topic

## How to sell well here

The short answer

Selling well in Gaston County comes down to three things: a price based on recent nearby sales, a home that is prepared and photographed for the way buyers shop, and paperwork done right, starting with North Carolina’s required disclosure statement. The guides below cover each step for sellers in Gastonia, Belmont, Mount Holly, Lowell and nearby towns.

Pricing is local. Two homes a few streets apart in Belmont or Mount Holly can sell very differently depending on age, condition, lot, school assignment and how close they sit to the Catawba River or downtown. That is why these guides talk about comparable sales and condition rather than countywide averages. Your county tax value is not a market price either: Gaston County sets tax values in a countywide reappraisal, and its next one values property as of January 1, 2027.

Preparation is where sellers have the most control. The guides cover what to repair before listing, decluttering, curb appeal and getting ready for professional photos, since buyers see the photos before they see the house.

The paperwork matters too. In North Carolina, sellers of most homes must complete the Residential Property and Owners’ Association Disclosure Statement and give it to the buyer no later than when the buyer makes an offer (N.C.G.S. 47E). In South Carolina, the Residential Property Condition Disclosure Statement is due before the contract is signed. North Carolina listing agreements must be in writing, and commissions are agreed between you and your brokerage; the Real Estate Commission does not set them.

When you are ready, start with a pricing consultation (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/home-value-in-gastonia-nc/>) . Ally prepares it by hand from recent nearby sales and a walk-through. You can also read how selling with Ally (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/sell-your-home-in-gastonia-nc/>) works, from preparation to closing.

Straight answers

## Questions readers ask

### What disclosure form do I give buyers in North Carolina?

Most sellers must complete the Residential Property and Owners’ Association Disclosure Statement (N.C.G.S. 47E) and give it to the buyer no later than the time the buyer makes an offer. Every question needs an answer, and if the form is not delivered in time the buyer may, under certain conditions, be able to cancel the contract. There are limited exemptions, such as new homes that have never been occupied.

### Is my Gaston County tax value what my home will sell for?

No. Tax values come from the county’s countywide reappraisal, which North Carolina requires at least every eight years. Gaston County’s last reappraisal was in 2023 and the next sets values as of January 1, 2027. A sale price depends on recent comparable sales and your home’s condition, which is what a pricing consultation (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/home-value-in-gastonia-nc/>) looks at.

### Who sets real estate commissions?

You and your brokerage, in a written listing agreement. The North Carolina Real Estate Commission does not set or regulate commission rates, and listing agreements must be in writing and signed when the agency relationship begins.

### What if my home is in South Carolina?

South Carolina sellers of most one- to four-unit homes must complete the state’s Residential Property Condition Disclosure Statement and deliver it before the buyer and seller sign the contract, unless the contract says otherwise.

Checked November 19, 2026 against: NCREC: Residential Property and Owners’ Association Disclosure Statement (<https://www.ncrec.gov/forms/consumer/rec422.pdf>) · NCREC: Buyer Agency Agreements (<https://bulletins.ncrec.gov/buyer-agency-agreements/>) · NCDOR: Types of property to be taxed (reappraisal) (<https://www.ncdor.gov/taxes-forms/property-tax/types-property-be-taxed>) · Gaston County: Real Estate Appraisal Department (<https://gastongov.com/661/Real-Estate-Appraisal-Department>) · Gaston County: We Value Gaston 2027 (<https://www.gastongov.com/1446/We-Value-Gaston-2027>) · SC Real Estate Commission: Residential Property Condition Disclosure Statement (<https://www.llr.sc.gov/re/recpdf/Property-Condition-Disclosure-Statement-06.2025.pdf>) . Details change, so confirm hours, dates and prices with each source before you go.

# Buying a Home in Gaston County

Pre-approval, touring, offers, inspections and closing for buyers.

About this topic

## How buying a home works here

The short answer

Buying a home in Gaston County follows a set path: get pre-approved, put your buyer agency agreement in writing, tour, make an offer on North Carolina’s standard Offer to Purchase and Contract, use the due diligence period to inspect and appraise, then close. The guides below explain each step for Gastonia, Belmont, Mount Holly and nearby towns, and for York County, SC across Lake Wylie.

Buying here means choosing between very different places close together: older mill-village streets in McAdenville and Cramerton, newer neighborhoods around Belmont and Mount Holly near the Catawba River, more land toward Dallas, Cherryville and Kings Mountain, and the South Carolina side of Lake Wylie in York County. Rules and costs change at the state line, so know which side you are shopping on before you start.

In North Carolina most resale homes are bought on the standard Offer to Purchase and Contract (Form 2‑T). It gives the buyer a negotiated due diligence period to arrange inspections, an appraisal, a survey and insurance quotes, in exchange for a due diligence fee paid to the seller. Earnest money is a separate deposit, usually held in a trust or escrow account. The North Carolina Real Estate Commission explains both in its consumer guides.

On the lending side, federal rules give you two documents to watch: a Loan Estimate within three business days of applying, and a Closing Disclosure at least three business days before closing. Comparing Loan Estimates side by side shows the real difference between lenders. Our preferred lender (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/our-preferred-lender/>) page and mortgage calculator (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/mortgage-calculator/>) help you get started.

Straight answers

## Questions readers ask

### Do I need a written agreement with a buyer’s agent in North Carolina?

Yes, before any offer. North Carolina Real Estate Commission rules require a buyer agency agreement to be in writing and signed no later than the time an offer is made, and the agreement should clearly state how your agent will be paid. You can sign it at the start so expectations are clear from the first showing.

### What is the difference between earnest money and a due diligence fee?

Earnest money is a good-faith deposit made with your offer. A due diligence fee is a separate, negotiated amount paid to the seller in exchange for your right to end the contract for any reason during the due diligence period. Due diligence fees usually go straight to the seller rather than into a trust account. See our earnest money guide (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/what-to-know-about-earnest-money-in-gastonia-nc/>) .

### When will I see my final loan costs?

Your lender must send a Loan Estimate within three business days of receiving your application, and you must receive the Closing Disclosure, with the final terms and closing costs, at least three business days before closing. Use those days to compare the two and ask about any changes.

### Is buying in South Carolina different?

In a few important ways. South Carolina sellers must give buyers the state’s Residential Property Condition Disclosure Statement before the contract is signed, and a home you live in as your primary residence can qualify for the 4% legal-residence assessment ratio for property tax if you apply with the county assessor.

# Gaston & York County Communities

Town and neighborhood guides across Gaston County, York County and Charlotte.

About this topic

## Getting to know the area

The short answer

Gaston County, NC and York County, SC sit west and south of Charlotte on either side of the state line, with towns from Gastonia, Belmont and Mount Holly to Clover, Fort Mill and Rock Hill. These guides compare them on the things that matter day to day: commute routes, schools, lake and river access, downtowns and the North Carolina vs. South Carolina differences.

Gaston County runs west from the Catawba River along I‑85 and US‑29/74 toward Kings Mountain and Crowders Mountain State Park, with US‑321 running north through Gastonia toward Dallas and Lincolnton. Belmont, Mount Holly, Cramerton and McAdenville sit closest to Charlotte along the Catawba and South Fork rivers. Across Lake Wylie, York County takes in Clover, Lake Wylie, York, Fort Mill and Rock Hill.

Schools are assigned by address. Gaston County Schools is the public school system for Gaston County. On the South Carolina side, York County is split between Clover School District, Fort Mill Schools, Rock Hill Schools and York School District 1, so check the district’s own attendance-zone tool for any address you are serious about.

Property taxes work differently in each state. In North Carolina you pay the county rate plus any city or town rate on the county’s assessed value. In South Carolina, a primary residence can qualify for a 4% assessment ratio if you apply with the county assessor. On Lake Wylie, Duke Energy manages the shoreline under its federal license, so most new docks, piers and shoreline work need a Duke Energy permit.

Straight answers

## Questions readers ask

### Which school district serves a Gaston County address?

Gaston County Schools is the public school district for Gaston County, and school assignments follow your address. In York County, SC, the district depends on where the home sits: Clover, Fort Mill, Rock Hill or York School District 1. Confirm any specific address with the district before you buy.

### How do property taxes differ between North Carolina and South Carolina?

In North Carolina, your bill is the county rate plus any city or town rate, applied to the county’s assessed value. In South Carolina, an owner-occupied primary residence can be assessed at 4% of fair market value instead of the higher rate for other property, but you have to apply with the county assessor.

### Do I need a permit for a dock on Lake Wylie?

Usually, yes. Duke Energy owns or controls the lakebed and manages the shoreline under its Federal Energy Regulatory Commission license, so new docks, piers, shoreline stabilization and many repairs need a permit from Duke Energy Lake Services. Check before you buy a waterfront lot.

# Gaston County Housing Market

Forecasts, pricing trends and what the numbers mean locally.

About this topic

## Reading the local market

The short answer

These market guides explain what is changing in Gaston County and York County housing and what it means for buyers and sellers, in plain language. They link the public sources they cite and are not MLS statistics. For recent sales near a specific home, ask Ally for a pricing consultation.

Housing markets move at the neighborhood level. Prices, days on market and the number of homes for sale can look very different in a Belmont subdivision, a Gastonia mill village, a lake community on Lake Wylie and a rural tract near Cherryville in the same month. Countywide headlines rarely tell you what your own home would sell for.

These articles focus on the forces behind local prices: demand from people who work in Charlotte, mortgage rates, the supply of homes for sale and new construction along corridors like I‑85 and US‑321. When they cite a number, they link the source, such as the U.S. Census Bureau’s QuickFacts or Freddie Mac’s weekly mortgage rate survey. Dates matter, so check each article’s published and updated dates.

Two numbers people often mix up are tax value and market value. Gaston County’s assessed values come from its countywide reappraisal; the last was in 2023 and the next sets values as of January 1, 2027. North Carolina law requires counties to reappraise at least every eight years. Market value comes from recent comparable sales and the home’s condition.

For a number you can act on, request a pricing consultation (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/home-value-in-gastonia-nc/>) . Buyers can read about buyer representation (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/buyer-agent-services-in-gastonia-nc/>) , and sellers about selling with Ally (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/sell-your-home-in-gastonia-nc/>) .

Straight answers

## Questions readers ask

### Are these market articles based on MLS data?

No. They explain trends in plain language and link the public sources they cite. They are not MLS statistics. For recent sales near a specific home, ask Ally for a pricing consultation (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/home-value-in-gastonia-nc/>) .

### How often does Gaston County reappraise homes for property tax?

North Carolina requires every county to reappraise real property at least every eight years, and some counties do it more often. Gaston County’s last countywide reappraisal was in 2023, and the next sets values as of January 1, 2027.

### Where can I check current mortgage rates?

Freddie Mac publishes national average rates every week in its Primary Mortgage Market Survey. The rate you are offered depends on your credit, down payment and loan type, so compare Loan Estimates from lenders; our mortgage calculator (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/mortgage-calculator/>) shows how a rate changes the monthly payment.

Checked November 19, 2026 against: NCDOR: Types of property to be taxed (reappraisal) (<https://www.ncdor.gov/taxes-forms/property-tax/types-property-be-taxed>) · Gaston County: Real Estate Appraisal Department (<https://gastongov.com/661/Real-Estate-Appraisal-Department>) · Gaston County: We Value Gaston 2027 (<https://www.gastongov.com/1446/We-Value-Gaston-2027>) · Freddie Mac: Primary Mortgage Market Survey (<https://www.freddiemac.com/pmms>) · CFPB: Review your Loan Estimates (<https://www.consumerfinance.gov/owning-a-home/compare/review-loan-estimates/>) . Details change, so confirm hours, dates and prices with each source before you go.

# Building a Custom Home in Gaston County

Land, custom builds, floor plans, finishes and upgrades.

About this topic

## Building a home, step by step

The short answer

Building a custom home in Gaston County starts with the land: confirm zoning, utilities or well and septic, and the survey before you buy a lot. Then choose a licensed builder (North Carolina requires a state general contractor license for projects of $40,000 or more), agree on plans and a written contract, and plan for permits through Gaston County Building Inspections.

Gaston County offers everything from wooded lots around Cherryville, Dallas and Stanley to infill lots in Gastonia and Belmont. The right lot depends on more than price: zoning, road frontage, whether city water and sewer reach it, soil for a septic system, any floodplain, and covenants or HOA rules all shape what you can build and what it will cost.

In North Carolina, a general contractor must hold a state license when a project is valued at $40,000 or more (G.S. 87‑1). You can look up any builder’s license with the NC Licensing Board for General Contractors before you sign. A clear written contract should cover plans and specifications, allowances, the draw schedule, change orders and the warranty.

Gaston County Building Inspections handles residential permit applications. Before applying, the county asks for a zoning permit (from the city or town planning office if the lot is inside city limits), well and septic permits if the home will use them, and other approvals listed in its permit packages.

Ally also runs Bohanan Construction (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/bohanan-construction/>) , which builds custom homes in Gastonia, so the building guides here look at both the build and how a home will sell later. Not sure building is right for you? Start with should I buy or build? (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/should-i-buy-or-build/>)

Straight answers

## Questions readers ask

### Does my builder need a license in North Carolina?

Yes, if the project is valued at $40,000 or more. North Carolina law (G.S. 87‑1) requires a state general contractor license at that level, and you can check a builder’s license with the NC Licensing Board for General Contractors.

### What do I need before applying for a building permit in Gaston County?

Gaston County lists the approvals to gather first: a zoning permit from the right zoning office (the city or town if the lot is inside its limits), well and septic permits if the home will use them, and the other items in its residential permit package for new homes.

### Should I buy an existing home or build?

It depends on your timeline, budget and how specific your must-haves are. Our buy-or-build guide (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/should-i-buy-or-build/>) compares the two, and the land guides above explain what to check on a lot before you commit.

Checked November 19, 2026 against: NC Licensing Board for General Contractors: FAQ for consumers (<https://nclbgc.org/faq-consumers/>) · Gaston County: Permit applications (<https://www.gastongov.com/224/Permit-Applications>) · Gaston County: FAQs (building permits) (<https://gastongov.com/faq.aspx>) . Details change, so confirm hours, dates and prices with each source before you go.

## Custom builds, start to finish

Ally is the business manager and designer at Bohanan Construction (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/bohanan-construction/>) , which builds custom homes in the area.

The Conrad: choosing the final details

Building (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/blog-realtor-in-gastonia-nc/topic/building/>) Kings Mountain, NCNo. 193

# What Makes a Great Guest Suite in Kings Mountain, NC

Privacy, a nearby bath, smart layout and practical touches: what makes a guest suite work for visitors, and for buyers when you sell, in Kings Mountain.

By Ally Bohanan (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/about-ally-bohanan/>) Published November 16, 20262 min read

In this article

- Which type of guest suite fits your home?
- What do guests appreciate most?
- How should the layout work?
- What touches make it feel special?
- How can you reflect Kings Mountain's character?
- What should you check before building one?
- How does a guest suite help when you sell?
- Frequently asked questions

The short answer

A great guest suite in Kings Mountain gives visitors privacy, a full bathroom close by, comfortable heating and cooling, good storage and lighting, and a layout away from the primary bedroom and noisy rooms. Whether it's a main-floor suite, a basement suite or a separate apartment, check permits and local rules before you build or count it as living space.

## Key takeaways

- Privacy and a nearby full bath matter most.
- Place the suite away from the primary bedroom and loud rooms.
- Main-level suites work well for older visitors and future one-level living.
- Separate apartments and kitchens may need permits and must meet local zoning.
- A flexible guest suite can double as an office or multigenerational space later.

A guest suite is about more than an extra bedroom. Done well, it lets visitors feel at home while giving everyone some privacy. It can also make your home more appealing to future buyers, especially those who host family often or plan for multigenerational living.

Here's what makes a guest suite work in Kings Mountain if you're building, renovating or comparing homes.

## Which type of guest suite fits your home?

| Type | Pros | Watch for

| Main-level suite | Easy for older guests; future one-level living for you | Noise near living areas

| Upstairs or bonus-room suite | Often more separated | Stairs; heating and cooling balance

| Basement suite | Privacy; room for a sitting area | Moisture, egress windows, light

| Detached or garage apartment | Most independence | Permits, zoning, utilities, cost

## What do guests appreciate most?

- A private bedroom big enough for a queen or king bed

- A full bathroom in the suite or right next to it

- Sound separation from the kitchen, media room and primary suite

- Comfortable temperature, ideally with separate zone control

- Storage: a real closet, a luggage spot and a few empty drawers

## How should the layout work?

- Put the suite away from the primary bedroom so both sides have privacy

- Let guests reach the bathroom without crossing main living areas

- Avoid shared walls with loud rooms where you can

- Add a small sitting area or desk if space allows

- Think about a separate entrance only if you want more independence

## What touches make it feel special?

- Layered lighting with dimmers and bedside lamps or sconces

- Blackout or room-darkening window treatments

- Plenty of outlets near the bed and desk, including USB charging

- Strong Wi-Fi and cell signal

- A small beverage station or space for a compact refrigerator

- Durable, easy-to-clean flooring

- A neutral palette that suits a range of guests

## How can you reflect Kings Mountain's character?

Kings Mountain has deep roots, from the 1780 Revolutionary War battle to its small, busy downtown and the Gateway Trail, per our Kings Mountain community page (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/kings-mountain/>) . A guest suite can nod to that setting with:

- Natural wood tones or reclaimed materials

- Colors drawn from the surrounding landscape

- Local art or photography

- Large windows or French doors to bring in light

Simple, timeless design usually ages better than trend-driven choices.

## What should you check before building one?

Kings Mountain straddles Cleveland and Gaston counties, so confirm which jurisdiction handles permits and zoning for your address. Before you start:

- Get permits for finished space, bathrooms and electrical work

- Ask whether a kitchen or separate entrance changes how the space is classified

- Check HOA rules if you're in a community with covenants

- Confirm basement bedrooms meet egress requirements

- Review rental rules if you might rent the space

Finished, permitted space is easier to count and appraise when you sell. Ally also runs Bohanan Construction (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/bohanan-construction/>) , a custom home builder in Gastonia, so she can talk through guest suite layouts during a build. See best upgrades to add during a build in Kings Mountain (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/best-upgrades-to-add-during-a-build-in-kings-mountain-nc/>) .

## How does a guest suite help when you sell?

A well-designed suite can appeal to buyers with visiting family, multigenerational households or a need for a home office. Stage it clearly as a guest suite with fresh bedding, towels and good lighting so buyers understand its purpose. For more on what buyers look for, see top features buyers want now (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/top-5-features-buyers-want-now-in-north-carolina/>) .

Shopping for a home with a guest suite in Kings Mountain? Talk With a Buyer's Agent.

Straight answers

## Frequently asked questions

### Does a guest suite add value to a home?

It can widen the home's appeal, especially to buyers with visiting family or multigenerational needs. How much it affects price depends on comparable sales and whether the space is permitted and finished well.

### Can I add a kitchen to my guest suite?

Possibly, but a full kitchen can turn the space into a separate dwelling under local rules. Check with the city or county planning office before you add one.

### Can I rent out my guest suite?

That depends on local zoning, any HOA rules and your insurance. Confirm all three before listing it as a rental.

# https://allybohananrealestate.com/how-to-choose-the-right-paint-finish-in-belmont-nc/

Title: How to Choose the Right Paint Finish in Belmont, NC
Summary: Flat, eggshell, satin or semi-gloss? A room-by-room guide to paint finishes that hold up to daily life in Belmont and look good to buyers.

Building (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/blog-realtor-in-gastonia-nc/topic/building/>) Belmont, NCNo. 192

# How to Choose the Right Paint Finish in Belmont, NC

Flat, eggshell, satin or semi-gloss? A room-by-room guide to paint finishes that hold up to daily life in Belmont and look good to buyers.

By Ally Bohanan (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/about-ally-bohanan/>) Published November 13, 2026Updated November 16, 20263 min read

In this article

- What's the difference between paint finishes?
- Which finish works in each room?
- How does Belmont's climate affect paint?
- How do you make finishes look polished?
- What should sellers paint before listing?
- Frequently asked questions

The short answer

For most Belmont homes, use flat on ceilings, eggshell in living and dining rooms and bedrooms, satin in hallways, kitchens and kids' rooms, and semi-gloss on trim, doors and bathrooms. Keep finishes consistent across open spaces and choose more washable sheens where humidity, pets and heavy traffic are part of daily life.

## Key takeaways

- Sheen affects durability, cleanability and how walls look in photos, not just style.
- Flatter finishes hide wall flaws; glossier finishes clean more easily but show imperfections.
- Satin and semi-gloss handle moisture better in kitchens, baths and laundry rooms.
- Use one wall finish through connected open spaces for a calmer look.
- Before listing, refresh scuffed high-traffic areas first.

Paint finish is one of the easiest choices to overlook, and one of the most noticeable once it's wrong. The sheen you choose affects how walls wear, how easily they clean, how light moves through a room and how the home looks in listing photos.

Belmont has everything from older homes in its historic districts to newer neighborhoods and properties near the Catawba River. Here's how to choose finishes that fit both the house and how you live in it.

## What's the difference between paint finishes?

Finishes run from no shine to very shiny. More sheen generally means more durability and easier cleaning, but it also shows wall flaws more clearly.

| Finish | Look | Durability | Best for

| Flat or matte | No shine, hides flaws | Lowest; hard to scrub | Ceilings, low-traffic formal rooms

| Eggshell | Soft, low sheen | Moderate | Living rooms, dining rooms, bedrooms, offices

| Satin | Gentle sheen | Good; wipes clean | Hallways, kitchens, kids' rooms, laundry rooms

| Semi-gloss | Noticeable shine | High | Trim, doors, cabinets, bathrooms

| Gloss | High shine | Highest | Accent features, cabinetry, railings

In older homes with plaster or uneven walls, flatter finishes are forgiving. In newer homes with smooth drywall, you have more flexibility.

## Which finish works in each room?

### Living rooms, dining rooms and bedrooms

Eggshell is the go-to. It softens light, hides minor flaws and still handles occasional wiping. In open great rooms that see more traffic, a low-sheen satin is a good alternative.

### Kitchens

Satin is usually the best balance: it handles grease and frequent cleaning without the glare of full gloss on large walls. Use semi-gloss on trim and any painted cabinetry.

### Bathrooms and laundry rooms

Choose satin or semi-gloss, ideally a moisture- and mildew-resistant product. These finishes resist humidity better than flat paint, which helps prevent peeling.

### Hallways, stairways and mudrooms

These walls take the most bumps from bags, pets and kids. Satin on walls and semi-gloss on trim, doors and railings makes cleanup easier.

### Ceilings

Flat or matte reduces glare and hides imperfections.

### Trim and doors

Semi-gloss gives a crisp edge against eggshell or satin walls and stands up to repeated cleaning.

## How does Belmont's climate affect paint?

North Carolina summers bring heat and humidity, and spring brings plenty of pollen. That affects how paint holds up indoors:

- Moisture: Kitchens, baths and laundry rooms need finishes that resist humidity and mildew.

- Dust and pollen: Washable finishes in entryways and near doors save repainting.

- Sun-filled rooms: Strong light shows sheen differences and touch-up marks more clearly.

- Sunrooms and enclosed porches: Temperature swings call for more durable products.

Good ventilation matters as much as the finish. A bathroom fan that actually vents outside protects any paint.

## How do you make finishes look polished?

- Stay consistent. Use the same wall finish across connected open spaces so the rooms read as one.

- Contrast walls and trim. Eggshell or satin walls with semi-gloss trim looks finished and intentional.

- Avoid high-gloss walls unless it's a deliberate design choice; they show every flaw.

- Test first. Paint a sample board and look at it in morning and evening light.

- Think about photos. Very shiny walls can create glare in pictures, while very flat finishes can look dull.

If you're building, decide finishes early with your builder so they match how each room will be used. Ally also runs Bohanan Construction (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/bohanan-construction/>) , a custom home builder in Gastonia, so she's used to thinking about finishes from both the design and the resale side.

## What should sellers paint before listing?

Buyers notice scuffed or dingy walls quickly, and they can read them as deferred maintenance. Before you list:

- Touch up or repaint high-traffic areas such as halls, stairways and entries.

- Repaint bold or very personal colors in a neutral tone.

- Refresh trim and doors with semi-gloss.

- Make sure bathrooms show no peeling or mildew.

- Keep leftover paint labeled for touch-ups during the listing.

Durable finishes also help during the sale itself, since showings, inspections and appraisals all add wear. For more prep ideas, see how to choose finishes that sell later in Belmont (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/how-to-choose-finishes-that-sell-later-in-belmont-nc/>) and our home staging guidance (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/home-staging/>) . If you're getting ready to sell, Request a Pricing Consultation and we'll talk through which updates are worth doing first.

## Frequently asked questions

### What paint finish is best for ceilings?

Flat is the usual choice because it hides imperfections and reduces glare. In bathrooms, some homeowners use a moisture-resistant ceiling paint instead.

### Can I use eggshell in a bathroom?

You can in a well-ventilated powder room, but satin or semi-gloss usually holds up better in full baths where showers create humidity.

### Should I repaint before listing my Belmont home?

Not always. Touching up scuffed high-traffic areas and painting bold or dated colors a neutral shade often gives the most impact. Ask your agent which rooms will matter most in photos and showings.

Title: What to Know Before Touring New Construction in Gastonia, NC
Summary: Before you walk into a Gastonia model home: register your agent, separate base price from upgrades, read the builder contract and plan your own inspections.

Building (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/blog-realtor-in-gastonia-nc/topic/building/>) Gastonia, NCNo. 191

# What to Know Before Touring New Construction in Gastonia, NC

Before you walk into a Gastonia model home: register your agent, separate base price from upgrades, read the builder contract and plan your own inspections.

By Ally Bohanan (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/about-ally-bohanan/>) Published November 10, 2026Updated November 16, 20263 min read

In this article

- Why should you bring your agent on the first visit?
- What's included in the base price?
- What questions should you ask on a model home tour?
- How should you choose a lot?
- How do builder contracts differ?
- Should you use the builder's lender?
- Do you still need an inspection on a new home?
- What's the next step?
- Frequently asked questions

The short answer

Before touring new construction in Gastonia, bring or register your own buyer's agent on the first visit, since many builders require it. Know that model homes show upgrades, so ask for the base price and included features in writing. Review the builder's contract, lender incentives, lot premiums, HOA plans and warranty, and schedule independent inspections during construction.

## Key takeaways

- Many builders require your agent to be with you, or registered, on your first visit.
- Model homes are usually full of upgrades; get the standard features list and price in writing.
- Builder contracts often differ from the standard North Carolina resale contract; read them carefully.
- Compare builder lender incentives with outside loan quotes.
- Independent pre-drywall, final and warranty inspections catch problems while the builder is responsible.

New construction is exciting: fresh floor plans, new systems and the chance to pick finishes. It also works differently from buying a resale home. Builders set their own pricing, contracts and processes, and the model home you walk into is designed to sell. Here's what to know before you tour new construction in Gastonia.

## Why should you bring your agent on the first visit?

Many builders require your agent to be with you, or registered, on your first visit to the community. If you walk in alone and sign the guest book, you may lose the ability to have your own representation for that home. The on-site sales representative works for the builder. Your agent works for you. Our buyer agent services (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/buyer-agent-services-in-gastonia-nc/>) explain what that looks like.

## What's included in the base price?

Model homes usually show many upgrades: flooring, cabinets, counters, lighting, trim and landscaping. Ask for:

- The standard features list in writing.

- The price of each upgrade you'd want.

- What's included with the lot: grading, landscaping, driveway, fencing.

- Any lot premium.

- Deadlines for choosing selections.

Some upgrades are cheaper to add later (paint, light fixtures, some hardware). Structural changes, extra outlets and plumbing changes are easier during construction.

## What questions should you ask on a model home tour?

| Topic | Questions

| Builder | How long have you built in the area? Can I see finished homes or talk to owners?

| Timeline | What's the estimated completion date, and what happens if it's delayed?

| Contract | Can I get a copy of the contract to review before signing?

| Deposits | How much is due, and when is it refundable?

| Incentives | Are incentives tied to your lender or title company?

| Warranty | What's covered, for how long, and how do I file a claim?

| Inspections | Can I hire independent inspectors during construction?

| Community | How many phases are planned? What amenities are coming, and when?

| HOA | What are the dues and rules, and when does the HOA transfer from the builder?

## How should you choose a lot?

- Drainage. Look at how water moves across the lot and neighboring lots.

- Orientation. Sun exposure for the yard, porch and main rooms.

- What's behind you. Future phases, roads, retention ponds or commercial land.

- Usable yard. Slope and easements can limit fences, patios and pools.

## How do builder contracts differ?

Builders typically use their own contracts rather than the standard North Carolina resale form. They often favor the builder on delays, changes and deposits. Read every page, ask your agent to walk through it, and consider having a real estate attorney review it.

## Should you use the builder's lender?

Builder incentives tied to a preferred lender can help with closing costs or rates. Still, get a quote from another lender and compare the full picture. Start with our preferred lender (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/our-preferred-lender/>) for a second estimate.

## Do you still need an inspection on a new home?

Yes. City and county inspections check code compliance, not workmanship. Consider:

- A pre-drywall inspection to see framing, wiring and plumbing.

- A final inspection before closing.

- A warranty inspection before your first-year warranty deadline.

If you're weighing a production home against a custom build, see should I buy or build (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/should-i-buy-or-build/>) .

## What's the next step?

Explore the area on our Gastonia page (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/gastonia/>) . Before your first model home visit, Talk With a Buyer's Agent so your representation is in place from the start.

## Frequently asked questions

### Do I need my own agent for new construction?

The builder's sales representative works for the builder. Your own agent can help you compare base prices, upgrades, incentives and contract terms. Check the builder's registration policy before your first visit.

### Should I use the builder's preferred lender?

Compare first. Builder incentives can be valuable, but get a loan estimate from another lender too and look at total cost, not just the incentive.

### When should I inspect a new-construction home?

Common checkpoints are before drywall, before closing and before the builder warranty's first-year deadline. Ask the builder in writing whether independent inspections are allowed.

### What is a lot premium?

An extra charge for a more desirable lot, such as a larger, wooded, cul-de-sac or view lot. Ask how premiums are set and compare lots carefully.

# https://allybohananrealestate.com/best-pantry-upgrades-for-modern-living-in-mcadenville-nc/

Title: Best Pantry Upgrades for Modern Living in McAdenville, NC
Summary: Practical pantry upgrades for McAdenville homes, from historic mill-village houses to new construction, and what each one does for daily life and resale.

Building (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/blog-realtor-in-gastonia-nc/topic/building/>) McAdenville, NCNo. 190

# Best Pantry Upgrades for Modern Living in McAdenville, NC

Practical pantry upgrades for McAdenville homes, from historic mill-village houses to new construction, and what each one does for daily life and resale.

By Ally Bohanan (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/about-ally-bohanan/>) Published November 7, 2026Updated November 16, 20263 min read

In this article

- What makes a pantry work well?
- Which upgrades give you the most for the money?
- How do you upgrade a small pantry in an older home?
- Which higher-end pantry features do buyers notice?
- Which pantry layouts work best?
- What should you do before listing?
- Frequently asked questions

The short answer

The pantry upgrades that make the biggest difference are the practical ones: adjustable shelves, pull-out drawers for deep spaces, good LED lighting and an outlet for small appliances. Coffee stations, a butler's pantry and stone counters suit higher-priced or newly built homes. Whatever you add should match your kitchen and your home's price range.

## Key takeaways

- Visibility and reach matter more than size. Drawers and pull-outs beat deep fixed shelves.
- Adding an outlet and LED lighting is low cost and changes how a pantry works.
- In older, smaller McAdenville homes, vertical storage and door racks make the most of a reach-in pantry.
- Save butler's pantries, beverage fridges and stone counters for homes where buyers expect them.
- Match the pantry's finishes to the kitchen so it looks like part of the design.

The pantry has become one of the hardest-working spaces in the house. It handles bulk shopping, small appliances, school snacks and the coffee setup. In McAdenville (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/mc-adenville/>) , homes range from compact historic mill-village houses to newer construction on the edges of town, so the right upgrade depends a lot on what you're starting with. Here are the upgrades that make the biggest difference for living in the home and for getting it ready to sell.

## What makes a pantry work well?

Three things: you can see everything, reach everything and keep it organized without effort. Square footage matters less than most people think. A small pantry that's well organized often works better than a big one with deep shelves where food gets lost.

## Which upgrades give you the most for the money?

| Upgrade | Cost level | What it solves

| Adjustable shelving | Low | Room for tall cereal boxes, small appliances and bulk packs

| Door-mounted racks | Low | Spices, wraps and small jars stored on space you weren't using

| LED or motion-sensor lighting | Low | Dark back corners, especially in interior pantries

| Pull-out drawers or baskets | Moderate | Deep shelves where items get lost

| A dedicated outlet | Moderate | Moves the toaster, air fryer and coffee maker off the counter

| Custom shelving or cabinetry | Higher | Awkward corners and a finished look that matches the kitchen

| Butler's pantry with counter and sink | Highest | Entertaining and keeping mess out of the main kitchen

## How do you upgrade a small pantry in an older home?

Many of McAdenville's older homes weren't built with walk-in pantries. To get more out of a reach-in:

- Run shelves all the way to the ceiling, and keep a step stool nearby for seldom-used items
- Use shallow shelves (about one can deep) on side walls so nothing hides behind anything else
- Put the heaviest items on the lowest fixed shelf or in floor-level drawers
- Add a rack to the back of the door
- Store items in clear, uniform bins and label them

If you're thinking about moving a wall or converting a closet, have a contractor check for wiring and plumbing first. That's common advice for any older home.

## Which higher-end pantry features do buyers notice?

In higher-priced homes, buyers expect the pantry to look as finished as the kitchen. Features that stand out:

- A coffee or beverage station with an outlet and a small counter
- Cabinetry and hardware that match the kitchen
- Quartz or stone counters for a prep area or appliance landing spot
- Beverage or wine storage in a butler's pantry between the kitchen and dining room
- Soft-close drawers

These features make sense when they fit the rest of the house. A marble-countered butler's pantry in a modest cottage won't return its cost. See what buyers expect at a luxury price point (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/what-buyers-expect-at-luxury-price-point/>) to check where your home falls.

## Which pantry layouts work best?

- U-shaped or L-shaped walk-in: the most storage per square foot, as long as the walkway stays clear.
- Butler's pantry: best placed between the kitchen and dining room, or near the garage entry.
- Corner pantry: angled shelves and a lazy Susan help make the corner usable.
- Cabinet pantry: tall pull-outs with full-extension drawers give the most usable space in the smallest footprint.

If you're building, decide where the pantry goes when you lay out the floor plan. Ally also runs Bohanan Construction (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/bohanan-construction/>) , which builds custom homes in Gastonia, and our buy or build guide (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/should-i-buy-or-build/>) compares the two paths.

## What should you do before listing?

If you're selling, you don't need a remodel. You need a pantry that photographs well and looks roomy:

- Remove expired items and anything stored on the floor
- Decant snacks and staples into matching containers, or at least group them neatly
- Replace dead bulbs, or add a plug-in or battery LED light
- Leave some open shelf space so buyers can see room to spare

For more pre-listing ideas, see the best value upgrades before selling in McAdenville (<https://allybohananrealestate.com/ally-bohanan-real-estate-preview/best-value-upgrades-before-selling-in-mcadenville-nc/>) . If you're planning a sale, Request a Pricing Consultation and Ally will tell you which updates are worth doing for your home.

## Frequently asked questions

### Can I add a pantry to a kitchen that doesn't have one?

Often, yes. A tall pull-out cabinet, a converted coat closet next to the kitchen or a wall of shallow floor-to-ceiling shelves can work. In older homes, have a contractor check for plumbing and wiring before you open a wall.

### Are walk-in pantries better than cabinet pantries?

Not automatically. A well-organized cabinet pantry with full-extension drawers can hold more usable storage than a dim walk-in with deep shelves. Plan around how you cook and shop.

### If I'm building, where should the pantry go?

Close to the kitchen work area and, ideally, on the path from the garage or side door so groceries go straight in. Settle this when you lay out the floor plan, not after framing.
